row.qualification: The printed repeated denominator pi_n is corrected to pi_m by a positive convergence theorem; no additional refutation is added. Existing uniqueness requires real roots placed in assigned original isolating discs, which are then proved to lie in the gaps. That premise is not explicit in the overview characterization, so its unrestricted uniqueness clause remains unresolved and this group is partial.

row.requirement: Unique entire psi function from its corrected literal product and normalized periods, without root placement or reality assumptions on the competing products
reviewed_claims: An entire numerator with sub-sine growth and zero periods around every actual gap vanishes. Real interpolation uses one zero in each open or collapsed gap; reflected real and imaginary parts extend it to arbitrary complex numerators.

Every deleted product with arbitrary complex lp displacements has the needed sub-sine growth on expanding half-integer circles. Equal periods therefore determine the entire function without root placement or root reality assumptions.

At every real source, one constructed family of circles works before all deleted indices. For each index exactly one function has the corrected literal symmetric product and normalized Kronecker periods. The same characterization holds for every admissible original winding-one piecewise C1 circuit family.
The statements hold for every finite p>1 and hence for the stated Hilbert case. All factors -2/pi_n and 1/(2*pi), mode-dependent denominators, signed indices and collapsed gaps are retained.
row.qualification: Uniqueness concerns the entire function, not an arbitrary enumeration of its roots. The corrected denominator pi_m is retained directly. The source potential is real, as in the Section 7 overview; no stronger arbitrary-complex-source uniqueness claim is inferred. No new refutation is added.

row.requirement: Angle conventions and the collapsed-gap locus
reviewed_claims: The actual real angle is defined modulo 2*pi on its open-gap locus, with local analytic representatives modulo pi.

The actual real Hilbert squared-gap zero set has a global analytic chart onto a closed coordinate plane of real codimension two. Its tangent space is the kernel of a surjective two-coordinate differential and equals the space of velocities of curves in the zero set.
row.qualification: The corrected real codimension is two. The original physical Hilbert space and squared-gap locus are retained; no complex codimension claim is inferred. Existing positive geometry supplies this comparison without a new counterexample.

row.requirement: Hilbert canonical Poisson relations
reviewed_claims: At the Hilbert exponent, the actual action derivatives commute; the angle/action bracket is the Kronecker delta and the angle/angle bracket vanishes on exactly the stated open-gap domains.
row.qualification: Specialize the finite-p theorem to p=2. The Fourier brackets are absolutely convergent pairings of actual derivatives, with frequency reversal and physical sign -i. Only gaps belonging to angle variables must be open; action gaps may be collapsed.

row.requirement: Rough Fourier-Lebesgue input and non-measure assertion
reviewed_claims: For every finite p>2, there is an actual real Fourier-Lebesgue source pair whose first original unit-period distribution is not represented by any complex measure.
The second component is the conjugate reflection of the first component coefficients, so the obstruction lies in the dissertation real source space.
row.qualification: The theorem reuses the existing non-measure distribution and supplies its real source pair. The sentence about standard ODE theory is motivation: no impossibility of every possible generalized fundamental-solution theory is asserted.

row.requirement: Entire product extension and agreement with classical discriminant
reviewed_claims: The corrected even spectral product plus two defines the actual source discriminant, jointly entire in the spectral parameter and finite-p source pair for p>1.

Above two it agrees with the physical Hilbert monodromy trace along the Hilbert inclusion; below two it is the restriction to the stronger source space. Classical finite Fourier agreement uniquely determines the jointly continuous extension.
row.qualification: The normalization is the already corrected parity product. The discriminant is not obtained by arbitrarily choosing a square root of the full product. All source norms and the direction of each exponent inclusion are retained.

row.requirement: Extended roots, actions, psi, anti-discriminant and density transfer
reviewed_claims: The canonical root is the limit of the actual root products and is analytic off the original cuts. The original contour action construction extends to every finite p>1 on a common complex neighborhood.

The normalized psi family and actual anti-discriminant are constructed; the latter is the difference of the two auxiliary characteristic products and agrees with the classical anti-trace at Hilbert inputs. The angle is the constructed path sum in S7-012.

The canonical relations hold for every finite p>1. Angle commutation above two follows through finite Fourier real sources and norm density; below two it follows by restriction of the actual regular cotangents.
row.qualification: This matches the mathematical construction and transfer claims, not a textual comparison with the exact cited 2014 procedure, which remains open. The separate unrestricted psi-characterization clause in S7-013 is not discharged here. Finite Fourier support in the density proof does not mean finitely many open gaps.

row.requirement: Theorem 7.1 common neighborhood and analytic actions
reviewed_claims: For each finite p>1 there is one open complex neighborhood containing the entire real source locus on which every indexed action is complex analytic, and hence real analytic.
The same constructed neighborhood also supports the open-gap angle phases and local representatives.
row.qualification: The neighborhood is common to all indices. No restriction to a bounded source set, finite number of indices or finite-gap sources is introduced.

row.requirement: Theorem 7.1 real mod-2pi angles and mod-pi extension
reviewed_claims: On the real open-gap locus, the actual angle is a Real.Angle class, with a unit-modulus exp(i*theta) phase. Its square is the complex analytic exp(2*i*theta) phase.
At every point of the complex open-gap domain there is a local analytic representative, real on real sources, whose differential is the actual angular differential.
row.qualification: The source wording is interpreted with its explicit modular conventions: real angles modulo 2*pi and complex analytic continuation modulo pi. No globally single-valued real representative or angle at a collapsed selected gap is claimed.

row.requirement: Theorem 7.1 exact canonical relations and domains
reviewed_claims: All three canonical identities hold for the same constructed family at every finite p>1 on precisely their source domains.

The brackets have literal absolutely convergent Fourier formulas using the actual action and angle differentials, frequency reversal and the factor -i. Action/action requires no open gap, angle/action requires only the angle gap, and angle/angle requires both angle gaps.
row.qualification: The actual regular cotangents identify these formulas with the source bracket above two and extend the literal convergent pairing below two. The range is strictly 1<p<infinity.

units.assessment_convention: Current ordered ledger; all historical supporting records retained.

row.requirement: Discriminant extension, classical full product and parity levels
reviewed_claims: The source discriminant is jointly analytic and agrees with the physical Hilbert monodromy trace. Its squared value minus four has the literal full endpoint product with prefactor -4.
The levels two and minus two are exactly the original even and odd parity spectra. For real sources the canonical endpoints have their index-prescribed signed levels.
row.qualification: The source period-one embedding retains the original operator domain and source norm. The opening roadmap for subsequent estimates and continuity is assessed in the later passage groups, not counted as a separate completed result here.

row.requirement: Complex parity labels, local central parity counts and distant identification
reviewed_claims: Intersecting the uniform circle and parity-count neighborhoods gives, for all sufficiently large M, exactly 4M+2 even-sector and 4M odd-sector eigenvalues inside radius (2M+1/2)*pi, counted with original algebraic multiplicity.
Distant counted pairs lie in their index parity. Separately ordering the two parity sequences preserves the distant pair multisets and actual central counts.
row.qualification: The common neighborhood is obtained by intersection and pullback along the continuous linear source embedding. Central parity lists are constructed independently; taking alternating slots of the globally sorted complex full spectrum is not assumed. No separate counterexample is added to this explanatory ordering warning.

row.requirement: Lexicographically ordered actual parity sequences and Hilbert displacements
reviewed_claims: Actual parity sequences can be sorted within each pair and between every two same-parity indices, without a real-type premise. Their displacements belong to l2 at Hilbert exponent.
Reindexing by 2n and 2n+1 gives the two displayed source lattices. Beyond both cutoffs, ordered-pair uniqueness identifies these slots with the corresponding globally ordered distant endpoints.
row.qualification: CompletePeriodicParityPairs retains central multisets and all distant multiplicities. The last identification uses the maximum of the chosen parity and canonical cutoffs. It does not assert a central cross-parity ordering or analytic individual root labels.

row.requirement: Equation (2.4) with corrected parity prefactors
reviewed_claims: The symmetric even product has prefactor -1 and limit Delta-2; the symmetric odd product has prefactor 4 and limit Delta+2. Both converge locally uniformly on the whole spectral plane.
row.qualification: These are the positive corrected formulas for (2.4), including pi_0=1. The new implementation adds no refutation of the printed constants.

row.requirement: Finite-p counted parity sequences and extension definition
reviewed_claims: At each finite p>1, one original open convex neighborhood supplies ordered actual parity lists with lp displacements at every sufficiently large cutoff.
The corrected even product plus two defines the source discriminant; the odd product gives the same value after subtracting two.
row.qualification: The reference to (2.4) uses the correction recorded in S8-004. Hilbert agreement is an extension above two and a restriction below two. The assertion does not include p=1 or infinity.

row.requirement: Lemma 8.1(i): parity product joint analyticity
reviewed_claims: Both corrected products are jointly complex analytic in the spectral parameter and the original potential, including at root collisions.
The printed scalar rescalings are analytic as well; analyticity alone is independent of their normalization.
row.qualification: The proof uses intrinsic symmetric polynomials and local uniform analytic approximation. It does not assume analytic eigenvalue coordinates. Compatibility with the trace uses the corrected constants in the next group.

row.requirement: Lemma 8.1(ii): corrected compatibility and unique extension
reviewed_claims: With prefactors -1 and 4, Delta=f+2=g-2 on the entire finite-p source domain.
Agreement with the classical discriminant on finite Fourier inputs uniquely determines the jointly continuous extension, hence the analytic extension.
row.qualification: The original norms and exponent inclusions are retained. The normalization correction is necessary for the shifted identities. No additional incompatibility proof is introduced.

row.requirement: Lemma 8.1(iii): uniform exterior trace and derivative asymptotics
reviewed_claims: For every tolerance, one original open convex neighborhood and positive threshold control the additive trace error and additive derivative error by epsilon*exp(abs(Im z)) throughout the original exterior.
The derivative quotient by -2*sin(z) converges uniformly to one there. The trace quotient is proved where 2*cos(z) has an explicit positive lower bound relative to exp(abs(Im z)).
row.qualification: The full exterior is unchanged for the additive trace estimate and sine quotient. The cosine quotient retains its denominator condition; it is not asserted uniformly across cosine zeros. Existing positive corrections are reused.

row.requirement: Lemma 8.1(iv): full product and periodic zero set
reviewed_claims: Delta squared minus four is the product of the corrected parity factors and the full symmetric endpoint product with prefactor -4.
Its zero set is exactly the original periodic spectrum, and its analytic zero order is the original algebraic multiplicity.
row.qualification: Both printed scalar rescalings cancel in their product, so this full-product normalization is unchanged. Coincident roots and central algebraic multiplicities are retained.

row.requirement: Finite even products, locally uniform convergence and trace asymptotic chain
reviewed_claims: Finite even cutoffs equal the normalized intrinsic central even polynomials at index 2M. These converge jointly locally uniformly to the corrected even product.
The ratio of the even product to 2*cos(z)-2 tends to one on the original exterior, locally uniformly in the potential. The resulting trace estimate is the additive estimate of S8-008.
row.qualification: The finite even product already has prefactor -1. Its limit is the corrected f. The last printed asymptotic-chain step is replaced by the proved additive trace estimate or by a cosine quotient with the stated denominator bound.

row.requirement: Original parity projection, finite rank and corrected determinant cutoff
reviewed_claims: The original resolvent contour projection restricted to a Fourier parity is analytic and has finite-dimensional range; its domain lift retains the original unbounded operator.

Every sufficiently large even cutoff equals minus the actual even contour determinant divided by its normalization at circle index 2M. The odd cutoff has factor 4 and retains its positive boundary pair 2M+1.
row.qualification: The circle radius is (2M+1/2)*pi for a product over even modes through 2M. Both the negative even prefactor and the doubled circle index are explicit. Callers of the source existence theorem supply neither contour admissibility nor hypothetical root sequences; both are constructed.

row.requirement: Analytic projection transport, conjugated determinant and limit analyticity
reviewed_claims: Local analytic projection transport conjugates the actual parity reduction to an operator on a fixed original finite-dimensional range, preserving the determinant.
The corrected normalized central parity polynomials are jointly analytic on a common neighborhood for all large cutoffs. Their locally uniform limit is jointly analytic on the full source domain.
row.qualification: The conjugated displayed even determinant keeps the same negative prefactor as S8-011. Transport is used locally for each fixed cutoff and point; the proof of common-neighborhood analyticity does not require one global trivialization for every cutoff. The odd intrinsic approximants remove the boundary factor only in the limit.

row.requirement: Compatibility by Hilbert agreement and source-norm density
reviewed_claims: Hilbert compatibility transfers below two by exact exponent inclusion, and above two by continuity on the dense Hilbert image. Finite Fourier density supplies uniqueness in the original source norm.
row.qualification: This is compatibility of the corrected products. Below two the direction is restriction to the stronger source space, not density of all Hilbert inputs in it.

row.requirement: Cauchy derivative estimate and exterior sine bound
reviewed_claims: Cauchy estimates on smaller exterior discs give the derivative error on the same original exterior. A positive uniform bound on exp(abs(Im z))/abs(sin z) converts it into the required sine quotient.
The implemented reciprocal-sine theorem supplies a finite constant depending only on the excluded-disc radius. Its explicit constant 4 is proved for abs(Im z)>=1.
row.qualification: The complete derivative conclusion is proved, but the literal intermediate constant 4 throughout the lower horizontal strip has not been established by this comparison. This is a remaining quantitative refinement, not a claim that the printed bound is false. No refutation is requested or added.

row.requirement: Cauchy derivative estimate and exterior sine bound
reviewed_claims: Cauchy estimates give the derivative error on the original exterior. The exact intermediate bound norm(cos(z)/sin(z)) <= exp(abs(Im(z)))/norm(sin(z)) <= 4 now holds throughout that exterior, including its lower horizontal strip.
The positive proof obtains norm(sin(z)) >= 1/2 outside all quarter-pi free discs and combines this with the exponential difference bound.
row.qualification: This resolves the quantitative refinement left partial by the preceding review. The integration example turns an additive error epsilon*exp(abs(Im(z))) into a quotient error at most 2*epsilon. No assertion that the printed constant is false is needed.

row.requirement: Full product factorization and actual algebraic multiplicities
reviewed_claims: The intrinsic parity factors multiply to the original full canonical product. Each parity factor has precisely its original algebraic zero orders; the full order is the original periodic algebraic multiplicity.
The determinant reduction retains the original generalized root chains, so multiplicity is not inferred only from a set-level root equality.
row.qualification: The source product argument is implemented through exact finite multiplicities and the canonical entire products. All spectral points, including repeated central roots, are covered.

row.requirement: Complex lexicographic discontinuity and Figure 2.1
reviewed_claims: In every original source neighborhood of zero there is a constant complex source at which both actual central periodic endpoint labels are discontinuous.
A continuous source curve makes two simple central roots cross a vertical line, changing the lexicographic choice as in Figure 2.1.
row.qualification: The existing witness theorem is reused. The source warning is existential for general complex potentials; it does not assert discontinuity at every complex source or at zero itself.

row.requirement: Lemma 8.2(i): endpoint continuity at real bases under complex perturbations
reviewed_claims: At every real-type original source, both ordered periodic endpoint maps are continuous at every signed index under arbitrary complex source perturbations.
The implementation also proves continuity of both full lp displacement sequences and one neighborhood controlling all coordinate changes.
row.qualification: No root simplicity, noncollapsed-gap or real-perturbation restriction is imposed. The full sequence-norm conclusion is stronger than the printed coordinatewise statement.

row.requirement: Lemma 8.2(ii): strict separation of successive real gap pairs
reviewed_claims: At each real-type source, the endpoints within a gap are weakly ordered and successive gaps are strictly separated at every integer index.
row.qualification: The within-gap inequality permits coincident endpoints. The strict inequalities between distinct gaps include central indices and remain valid when either neighboring gap collapses.

row.requirement: Local endpoint discs, Rouche counts and ordered endpoint identification
reviewed_claims: Joint continuity gives locally uniform periodic products and stable analytic counts on every spectral-free circle near the source. Compact root confinement keeps nearby roots inside neighborhoods of the old spectrum.
Stable prefix and suffix counts in real-diameter discs bound the real part of each ordered slot. Imaginary-part confinement then gives complex coordinate continuity even at repeated endpoint values.
row.qualification: The formal proof uses real-diameter barriers to implement the source small-disc ordering argument. Counts are analytic multiplicities, not just the number of distinct root values. The continuous original embedding pulls the neighborhood back to the source norm.

row.requirement: Real order, signed levels (2.5) and distinct gaps
reviewed_claims: The real ordered endpoints have the signed discriminant level (-1)^n*Delta=2 for every positive, zero and negative index.
Adjacent pairs have opposite levels, yielding strict separation; lexicographic order reduces to the real order at real-type sources.
row.qualification: The signed level identity retains integer powers and the original source potential. Both restriction below exponent two and extension above it have already been justified in the discriminant compatibility comparison.

row.requirement: Closed-gap definition and exact discriminant superlevel characterization
reviewed_claims: The closed source gaps are exactly the real points where norm(Delta) is at least two; their interiors are exactly the points where it is greater than two.
On gap n the signed value (-1)^n*Delta is at least two, with a strict inequality in every nonempty gap interior. Equality in modulus occurs exactly at an endpoint.
row.qualification: The product-sign and level-continuity proof supplies the superlevel characterization directly. Collapsed gaps are included as singletons and each superlevel point belongs to exactly one gap.

row.requirement: Lemma 8.3: local uniform critical-root counts, exhaustion and reality
reviewed_claims: One open convex original neighborhood and positive cutoff give exactly one simple critical root in each distant quarter-pi disc, exactly 2K+1 central roots for every larger cutoff K, and exhaustion of all roots.
The distant and central boundaries are zero-free; central labels retain analytic multiplicity. At real-type sources every critical root is real.
row.qualification: The central circle used in the printed proof and the earlier height-K central box select the same critical roots after increasing the cutoff. Reality is supported by the real-rooted full-product derivative argument, not merely conjugation symmetry.

row.requirement: Rouche proof for distant and central critical-root counts
reviewed_claims: The locally uniform exterior derivative ratio supplies a strict Rouche inequality with tolerance one half on all sufficiently distant free circles and all sufficiently large central circles.
The free derivative counts transfer as one and 2K+1, with boundary nonvanishing. Exterior nonvanishing and the free-disc geometry exclude any further critical roots.
row.qualification: The same source neighborhood and cutoff work for every larger central circle, including both signed distant tails. Exhaustion is proved, rather than inferred from a single central count.

row.requirement: Real critical roots and extrema in all real gaps
reviewed_claims: The band to the right of gap n is (lambda_n^+,lambda_(n+1)^-). It is nonempty, and the discriminant real part has square strictly below four there.

Each real gap contains a critical point: Rolle supplies one in an open gap and endpoint multiplicity covers a collapsed gap. Distinct gap witnesses saturate the central critical multiset and identify the canonical indexed roots.
row.qualification: Printed p.50 gives the right-hand band endpoint with index n-1; the proved replacement uses n+1. The square bound is stronger than the needed signed upper bound. This is a positive correction, with no additional refutation theorem.

row.requirement: Locally uniform bounded critical-root displacement
reviewed_claims: The complete canonical critical sequence has a locally uniform bound on its displacement from pi*n, over all signed indices.
row.qualification: The later proved full lp displacement bound implies the displayed O(1) estimate by the coordinate norm bound. Central roots are included through a bounded finite head, and the same source neighborhood controls all indices.

row.requirement: Lemma 8.4: sampled l-p errors and Cauchy derivative estimate
reviewed_claims: For every sampler in the quarter-pi free discs, the actual trace and derivative errors form lp sequences with one locally uniform norm bound.
One majorant on the half-pi discs gives the trace estimate; Cauchy on the quarter-pi discs gives the derivative factor 4/pi.
row.qualification: The majorant is selected before the spectral sampling points. No continuity of the sampler or of the complex endpoint labels is assumed. Closed quarter-pi discs are covered, including their centers.

row.requirement: Lemma 8.5: ordered critical labels, literal derivative product and real-base continuity
reviewed_claims: The actual critical roots admit a complete lexicographic enumeration with exact multiplicities and locally uniformly bounded lp displacement.
The literal symmetric product with prefactor two and pi_0=1 converges locally uniformly on the whole spectral plane to the derivative. Each coordinate is continuous at real-type sources.
row.qualification: Sorting changes only a finite central block and preserves the distant labels. The norm estimate includes that entire central block; no globally continuous labeling at arbitrary complex sources is assumed.

row.requirement: Critical-root displacement from sampled derivative errors and the sine bound
reviewed_claims: At a distant critical root the sampled derivative-error estimate bounds sin(lambda_n^bullet). The inverse sine estimate on its free disc then bounds lambda_n^bullet-pi*n by an lp majorant.
A bounded finite central replacement produces a full lp displacement sequence with a common neighborhood norm bound.
row.qualification: The printed intermediate assertion is sin(lambda_n^bullet) in lp, not lambda_n^bullet itself. The exact free derivative factor -2 is retained in the bound and absorbed only into the final lp coefficient.

row.requirement: Entire critical product, removable quotient and asymptotic identification
reviewed_claims: The normalized entire critical product has the same finite analytic zero orders as the discriminant derivative, so their quotient extends across all common zeros.
The quotient tends to one on the free-disc exterior. Maximum modulus yields a global bound, and Liouville plus an escaping exterior sequence makes the quotient identically one.
row.qualification: The proof explicitly bridges the exterior asymptotic to the whole plane. Root-set equality alone is not used to infer removability; central repeated roots retain their full analytic orders.

row.requirement: Rouche continuity of critical labels
reviewed_claims: Locally uniform derivative dependence preserves critical counts on each zero-free circle. Ordered prefix and suffix barriers and imaginary-part confinement give coordinate continuity at real-type sources.
row.qualification: The proof parallels the periodic-endpoint count argument under arbitrary complex perturbations. At real type every critical root is simple, so the implementation also obtains local coordinate analyticity.

row.requirement: Unique strict gap extrema, including collapsed gaps
reviewed_claims: Every canonical critical root of a real source lies in its indexed closed gap and is the unique critical point there.
All such critical roots are simple zeros of the derivative and hence strict real local extrema, including collapsed gaps. There are no other real local extrema.
row.qualification: Strictness is expressed on a punctured real neighborhood, so it remains meaningful at a singleton gap. The proof combines exact global multiplicities, central count saturation, the second-derivative test and Fermat's theorem.

row.requirement: Lemma 8.6: locally uniform squared-gap critical offset
reviewed_claims: One open convex original neighborhood and one positive cutoff give the actual critical midpoint offset as the squared gap times an lp coefficient sequence with a uniform norm bound.
row.qualification: The statement is for arbitrary complex sources at every finite p>1. It includes all sufficiently distant signed indices and collapsed gaps; the finite central extension of the coefficient is zero.

row.requirement: Deleted product and corrected midpoint factorization
reviewed_claims: The deleted endpoint product has the literal outer factor 1/pi_n^2 and omits exactly the nth pair; its cutoffs converge locally uniformly on the whole plane.
With that normalization the exact midpoint factorization is Delta^2-4=-4*((tau_n-z)^2-gamma_n^2/4)*Delta_n(z).
row.qualification: The positive correction is the prefactor -4. The normalization includes pi_0=1, the removed index, coincident endpoints and evaluations at removed roots. Historical refutations are left unchanged; none is added.

row.requirement: Uniform deleted-product estimate and evaluation at the critical root
reviewed_claims: The deleted product differs from the squared filled free sine quotient by a locally uniformly bounded lp majorant on every half-pi disc.
At the actual distant critical roots, the deleted-product value minus one and its derivative have bounded lp tail representatives on one common source neighborhood.
row.qualification: The critical displacements and centered sine-quotient estimates control evaluation at moving roots. Central indices are filled by finite modification for full lp membership; local tail norm bounds are asserted on a common cutoff.

row.requirement: Cauchy derivative control and integral sinc identity
reviewed_claims: Cauchy converts the deleted-product value majorant on half-pi discs into a derivative majorant with factor 4/pi on quarter-pi discs.
The filled sinc equals the integral from zero to one of cos(s*z), including at z=0. After translation and squaring, its value error and derivative are O(z-pi*n) uniformly on fixed-radius free discs.
row.qualification: The new integral identity supplies the literal source display at its removable center. The derivative estimate is proved through entire increment bounds and the vanishing center derivative; the integration example verifies this for the literal squared integral.

row.requirement: Differentiated factorization, nonzero tail denominator and squared-gap conclusion
reviewed_claims: Differentiating the corrected factorization at a critical point gives 2*a*G(c)+(a^2-gamma^2/4)*Gprime(c)=0. Thus B*a=gamma^2*Gprime(c)/4 for B=2*G(c)+a*Gprime(c).

The coefficient error B-2 has locally bounded lp tail representatives. Independent uniform smallness estimates give norm(B)>=1 on a common tail, so a=gamma^2*Gprime(c)/(4*B) with locally bounded lp coefficients.
row.qualification: The common factor -4 cancels from the zero differentiated equation. Dividing the coefficient equation by two gives the printed normalized (1+lp) form. Uniform nonvanishing is proved separately from bounded lp norms, and only B is divided by, never the gap.

units.assessment_convention: Current ordered ledger; all historical supporting records retained.

row.requirement: Ordinary Dirichlet physical monodromy, zeros and the literal negative product.
reviewed_claims: The ordinary Dirichlet characteristic is the literal physical monodromy expression (m4+m3-m2-m1)/(2i) for every Hilbert source.
Its zeros are exactly the actual interval Dirichlet spectrum, with analytic zero order equal to algebraic multiplicity. The canonical symmetric product has prefactor -1 and denominator pi_0=1.
row.qualification: Physical agreement is proved by finite Fourier density and continuity, without a continuous-representative hypothesis. The entire function is normalized, not just its zero set. Every central and repeated root is retained.

row.requirement: Ordinary Neumann physical monodromy, zeros and the literal negative product.
reviewed_claims: The ordinary Neumann characteristic is the literal monodromy expression (m4-m3+m2-m1)/(2i), with the opposite separated endpoint sign.
The same actual-spectrum, multiplicity and negative-product statements hold for the complete Neumann root sequence.
row.qualification: The common BoundaryCondition argument is instantiated with neumann. This preserves the physical endpoint domain and the exceptional zero-mode denominator.

row.requirement: Extension from Hilbert sources using asymptotic spectral products.
reviewed_claims: The normalized boundary products extend to every finite source exponent p>1. They agree with the physical Hilbert characteristics in the appropriate exponent-inclusion direction.
Agreement on finite Fourier sources uniquely determines the continuous extension for each spectral parameter.
row.qualification: Above two this is extension from Hilbert sources; below two it is restriction along the inclusion into the Hilbert space. No assertion that all Hilbert sources belong to a stronger source space is made.

row.requirement: Lemma 9.1(i): joint analyticity, exact ordinary products and spectra.
reviewed_claims: Both actual ordinary characteristic functions are jointly analytic in the spectral parameter and original complex source.

Their literal symmetric root products converge locally uniformly on the whole spectral plane at each fixed source, and their zeros and analytic orders are exactly the actual spectra and algebraic multiplicities.
row.qualification: Joint analyticity is proved by uniform approximation with intrinsic central polynomials on actual Banach neighborhoods, then composition with the original interval extension. This does not assert joint local uniformity for lexicographically labeled finite cutoffs.

row.requirement: Lemma 9.1(ii): continuity at each real-type base.
reviewed_claims: Each ordinary signed boundary coordinate is continuous at every real-type source under arbitrary complex source perturbations.
The implementation also proves continuity in the full lp displacement norm and one source neighborhood controlling all signed coordinates of both ordinary sequences.
row.qualification: The coordinate result includes the finite central block. No global continuity of lexicographic labels at arbitrary complex bases is assumed.

row.requirement: Lemma 9.1(iii): ordinary Dirichlet and Neumann roots in their indexed periodic gaps.
reviewed_claims: At real-type sources both ordinary roots at index n lie in the original closed periodic gap n, with strict separation from the neighboring gaps.
The endpoints may coincide. In a collapsed gap either boundary root equals the common endpoint.
row.qualification: The chain is lambda_(n-1)^+ < lambda_n^- <= mu_n,nu_n <= lambda_n^+ < lambda_(n+1)^-. It places no ordering between mu_n and nu_n and covers every integer index.

row.requirement: Proof of Lemma 9.1: analytic products, Rouche continuity and transported signed discriminant levels.
reviewed_claims: Joint analytic approximation supplies the product argument omitted in the source. Stable Rouche prefix and suffix counts and imaginary-part confinement give the real-base coordinate continuity.
The indexed gap inequalities are transferred from real finite Fourier approximants using continuity. The signed discriminant level at either boundary root follows on that original indexed gap.
row.qualification: The proof retains the original gap index through approximation; the unsigned or signed superlevel condition alone would not identify it. The continuity proof permits complex perturbations and counts multiplicities.

row.requirement: Auxiliary analogues and the two physical monodromy displays.
reviewed_claims: Both actual auxiliary characteristics have the same joint analyticity, literal negative products, exact spectra and zero multiplicities. At real-type sources their coordinates are continuous and lie in the same original indexed periodic gaps.
The physical monodromy display with +i(m3+m2) is the actual Neumann* characteristic; the display with -i(m3+m2) is the actual Dirichlet* characteristic.
row.qualification: The correction preserves the endpoint-domain labels defined on printed p.33. Phase conjugation preserves periodic spectrum and multiplicities; ordered spectral-data uniqueness preserves the gap indices. The existing positive normalization identities are reused; no new counterexample or refutation is added.

row.requirement: Anti-discriminant as the monodromy off-diagonal sum and auxiliary difference.
reviewed_claims: The anti-discriminant is the actual physical monodromy off-diagonal sum m2+m3.
With the original endpoint-domain labels its auxiliary expression is actual Neumann* minus actual Dirichlet*. This is the difference of the printed plus and minus monodromy expressions.
row.qualification: This is the same auxiliary-label correction as S9-008, applied to the difference formula. The printed algebra is valid if its symbols denote the printed expressions, while the domain-consistent symbolic difference is N*-D*.

row.requirement: Lemma 9.2(i): analytic extension of the anti-discriminant.
reviewed_claims: The normalized anti-discriminant is jointly analytic on the entire original complex source space at every finite p>1.
Physical Hilbert agreement in both exponent directions and finite Fourier uniqueness fix the exact function.
row.qualification: The legacy name sourceAntiDiscriminantCandidate denotes the proved normalized extension. Equality is literal, not only equality of squares or zeros.

row.requirement: Lemma 9.2(ii): discriminant identity at simple Dirichlet roots.
reviewed_claims: At every actual ordinary Dirichlet zero, Delta(z)^2-4 equals delta(z)^2.
The identity is also instantiated at every canonical signed Dirichlet coordinate.
row.qualification: The implementation strengthens the source simple-eigenvalue assertion to all zeros, including multiple zeros, by substituting into the global characteristic identity.

row.requirement: Lemma 9.2(iii): locally uniform full value and derivative sample sequences in lp.
reviewed_claims: The full actual value and derivative sample sequences delta(mu_n) and deltaPrime(mu_n) are lp elements.
At each arbitrary complex source one open neighborhood and one finite norm bound control both complete sequences for every nearby source.
row.qualification: These are the actual canonical samples, including all central indices. The full-sample neighborhood is not required to be convex or contain zero; neither condition is stated in the source.

row.requirement: Proof of analytic extension by the auxiliary difference.

units.assessment_convention: Current ordered ledger; all historical supporting records retained.

Mixed central-tail separation and a positive central margin yield all-index quantitative separation. Connected source balls and their union through the connected real-type locus give the local and global connectedness.

row.qualification: All central and negative indices are included. Gap containment and disjoint disks discharge the branch exclusion; no large-index restriction or enlarged constant occurs.

reviewed_claims: Use the selected root w_n along G_n in Lemma 10.4.
For continuous f on the actual noncollapsed gap, one attained maximum bounds every stopping point on both sides. The literal real supremum is bounded by the data supremum.
The constant is exactly one, attained for constant data.

The actual coefficient Q_k=k^2 times the square-root correction obeys |Q_k| <= |gamma_k^2|/(2*pi^2) once the index dominates the midpoint displacement and spectral radius.

One source neighborhood and cutoff give this actual-gap bound simultaneously for all nearby sources and every spectral parameter in a prescribed bounded region. Hence compact spectral sets are covered.

reviewed_claims: The actual quadratic remainder sequence belongs to l(p/2), including when p/2 is below one; finite central coefficients are retained.

There are actual coefficients L in lp and R in l(p/2) with a_k+a_-k=L_k/k+R_k/k^2, and the sum can also be written as one lp coefficient divided by k.

The linear and cross contributions give absolutely summable paired deviations. Literal symmetric products converge locally uniformly, with a common vanishing bound on arbitrary finite tail subsets for nearby sources and bounded spectral parameters.

Deleting any signed index changes only finitely many factors. Analytic finite cutoffs and their locally uniform limit prove joint analyticity on the same common domain; nonzero factors and summable deviations prove nonvanishing.
row.qualification: The existing proof-index correction is reused positively. Absolute convergence is for paired blocks. The earlier l2/Holder route proves summability, while the new theorem additionally supplies the literal l(p/2) and l(p/4) coefficients. The same source domain and fixed local family are preserved.

reviewed_claims: The displacement parameter is exactly the full affine space sigma_m=pi*m+a_m with a in lp, without ordering, distinctness or smallness restrictions.

The quotient is jointly analytic in the spectral variable, every displacement sequence and the source on the printed closed-disk domain. The same W,V,D,c are retained, and the moving-gap domain and entire selected disk are also covered.
Literal cutoffs converge locally uniformly in all three variables, including numerator zeros and collisions.

The product identity and analyticity are asserted on the natural nonzero-denominator domain; numerator nonvanishing is not required.

row.requirement: Discriminant square identity and canonical root (2.13).

On the complement of all actual closed gaps its square is the actual discriminant squared minus four, and consequently Delta^2-4=-4*w_n^2*f_n^2.
row.qualification: The radicand square identity is asserted off all gaps; the product factorization itself is totalized and valid everywhere. Boundary-square identities are proved separately on selected gap sides. The free value at pi/2 is -2*i, fixing the branch sign. Symmetric pairing is retained.

row.requirement: Lemma 10.7: spectral and joint canonical-root analyticity.
reviewed_claims: Spectral analyticity holds on the complement of the actual full gap union at every original complex source.
Joint analyticity and local uniform convergence hold on the open moving-gap domain over the same W. The printed complement of the union of closed fixed disks uses exactly the previous V,D,c.
Corollary 10.6 is retained without a further shrinking or replacement of its common source domain.
row.qualification: The closure bar over U_m is present on rendered p.58. The canonical domain is proved open as the intersection of the omitted-zero and omitted-one domains. No analyticity of individually ordered endpoints is assumed.

row.requirement: Collapsed canonical roots and opposite side values (2.14).
reviewed_claims: At a collapsed gap the canonical root is exactly 2*i*(tau_n-z)*f_n and is analytic throughout the original selected disk.

At a noncollapsed gap, actual approaches from either oriented open side tend to opposite boundary values. These values are continuous on the closed coordinate interval and both vanish at the endpoints.
The side values square to the discriminant radicand; the original isolation data discharge avoidance of every other gap. The assertions apply at complex sources on the same W.
row.qualification: Collapsed analyticity is a fixed-source assertion, as printed; it does not claim a joint extension through nearby reopened gaps. Noncollapsed side approaches are oriented by the complex half-gap. Endpoints have value zero; strict nonzero signs concern the interior.

row.requirement: Figure 2.4: canonical-root signs on and around real gaps.
reviewed_claims: For every real-type source and every signed index, upper/lower gap values have real signs +(-1)^n and -(-1)^n.
On the adjacent open bands the canonical root is purely imaginary, with signs +i*(-1)^n before the gap and -i*(-1)^n after it.
The parity applies to negative and central indices, and the adjacent bands remain nonempty when a neighboring gap collapses.
row.qualification: Figure 2.4 displays phases, not unit magnitudes. Gap sign assertions require a noncollapsed real gap and interior parameter. Adjacent-band signs use the actual bands between consecutive indexed endpoints, with the implementation proving (-1)^|n|=(-1)^n.

reviewed_claims: The error is the literal finite least upper bound of the unordered quotient product minus one over every original disk, including the central disks.

For 1<q<infinity it has an exact lq+l(p/2) decomposition. For q=1 there is one fixed l(p/2)+l(1+) pair, chosen before every projection exponent. A zero third component gives the displayed three-term class.
The same common source domain and original disk family are chosen before numerator displacements and target exponents. Estimates are uniform on explicitly bounded lq offset families.
Correct the unrestricted local-uniformity assertion: q>=p, including infinity, retains the original lp topology; for q

row.requirement: Free-sine consequence of Lemma 10.8.
reviewed_claims: The free numerator gives the literal filled sine quotient divided by the same omitted standard-root product on every original disk.
The actual midpoint displacement has locally uniform refined bounds. They produce one l(p/2)+l(1+) supremum decomposition, with the two summands chosen before all l(1+) projection exponents.
Taking the lq component to be zero supplies the printed consequence for every q>=1. The local source neighborhood is chosen before those exponents.

row.requirement: Separation estimate for the squared half-gap correction.
reviewed_claims: Every original isolating disk satisfies the literal squared-gap radicand bound |gamma_m|^2/(4*|tau_m-z|^2) <= c^2*|gamma_m|^2/(4*|m-n|^2).
The same supplied separation constant c and disk family work for all sources in the given neighborhood and all distinct signed indices.

row.requirement: Uniform smallness split into far and near frequency differences.

When |m-n|>=|n|/2 and n is nonzero, c^2*|gamma_m|^2/(4*|m-n|^2) <= c^2*||gamma||p^2/|n|^2.
When m differs from n and |m-n|<|n|/2, the same term is at most (c^2/4)*||R_floor(|n|/2) gamma||p^2. The actual truncated sequence retains both signs of the index.

Actual lp gap tails are uniformly small on one source neighborhood. The full reciprocal-square row is uniformly small for all sufficiently distant omitted indices, hence every individual radicand is at most one half.
row.qualification: This is a positive norm correction. The new near estimate is stronger by its retained factor one quarter. Uniform smallness uses the already proved common tail control and the full-row argument, not bounded lp norms alone. The finite cutoff may be enlarged to exclude n=0.

The infinite midpoint product is an actual unordered product. Its signed reciprocal row and quadratic product remainder give the lq disk supremum for finite q>1 and every finite exponent above one when q=1.
The full quotient majorants preserve each original central disk using a separate compact bound, and retain explicit dependence on the lq midpoint offset norm.
row.qualification: The coefficient bound is pointwise for each admissible offset, and uniform on bounded offset families. The source topology correction is recorded in S10-033 and S10-040. Auxiliary empty central disks are used only for tail adapters; the final quotient retains the original nonempty central disks.

row.requirement: Inverse-square-root estimate for each small factor.

Its finite product estimate is exp(sum |x_m|)-1, with the literal constant one. Combined with the original-disk radicand estimate and uniform smallness, it supplies the displayed half-unit correction bound.

Choosing the actual midpoints as numerator roots identifies the literal unordered product of inverse-square-root corrections on the omitted-gap domain.

On every distant original disk, the literal product error has one uniformly bounded half-exponent majorant. Its actual least-upper-bound sequence is in l(p/2), including exponents below one, with a common source-neighborhood norm bound.

The literal sum over all signed indices of |a_n|^p is locally uniformly bounded. At every collapsed gap, including central complex gaps, the critical root equals the midpoint.

On every original isolating family the deleted product is nonzero at the indexed critical point. At a collapsed gap, spectral exhaustiveness and disjoint disks identify that root with the common endpoint; at an open gap, the quadratic identity supplies the nonzero coefficient.

row.requirement: Derivative-to-canonical-root product (2.15).
reviewed_claims: The actual discriminant derivative divided by the canonical root equals -i times the full product of (critical_m-z)/w_m(z), over every signed index, off all periodic gap segments.
Individual factor deviations from one are absolutely summable. The full product is an unordered HasProd, and literal symmetric cutoff products converge to the same normalized quotient.

Inserting one selected factor into the omitted product retains the exact normalization even if a numerator factor is zero. The product theorem strengthens the preceding Lemma 10.10 package on the unchanged common W.
row.qualification: The normalized quotient identity is asserted off the full gap union. Absolute summability also holds for the totalized factors at other spectral points, but no quotient identity on a removed gap is inferred. The argument never divides by a critical numerator factor.

row.requirement: Quotient analytic domains and admissible-path definition.

For any continuous complex path with arbitrary endpoints, admissibility means exactly that every strictly interior parameter avoids every periodic gap. Endpoints may belong to gaps. This definition requires no differentiability, integrability, disk-containment or half-plane premise.
row.qualification: The geometric definition applies to arbitrary continuous Path values. Smoothness and integrability belong to the later integral statements and are not built into admissibility. This comparison does not yet discharge Lemma 10.11 or Figure 2.5.

row.requirement: Figure 2.5: multiple admissible endpoint paths.

SourceAdmissiblePath imposes only avoidance of every indexed gap at strictly interior parameters. It has no simplicity, injectivity, straightness or half-plane premise.

The finite piecewise interior-C1 path class permits arbitrary intermediate vertices and pieces, including corners, repeated points and loops. Its source admissibility checks both piece interiors and genuine interior vertices.
row.qualification: Figure 2.5 is compared as an illustration of the admissible path class. The source supplies no parametrizations of its two drawn curves; this row does not claim a reconstruction or an existence theorem for those specific shapes. The later zero-integral assertion is a separate pending comparison.

row.requirement: Lemma 10.11(i): extension through every collapsed gap.
reviewed_claims: One function, -i times the unconditional product with every collapsed factor filled by one, extends the actual discriminant derivative divided by the canonical root.

For every complex source in the unchanged common W and every finite p>1, the extension is analytic on the complement of the union of all noncollapsed gap segments and agrees with the actual quotient off all gaps.

The enlarged domain is an open union of the original cut complement and the omitted domains of every collapsed index. The single function agrees with the omitted analytic product on each of these domains, including every original collapsed disk.
All signed indices, the central gap and infinitely many collapsed gaps are included. Absolute summability of the regularized factor errors proves that the displayed product converges unconditionally.
row.qualification: The analytically continued function is distinct from totalized division at a collapsed endpoint; agreement with the raw quotient is asserted on its original gap complement. The construction retains W and all original disks. Part (ii) and the separate displayed proof passages remain pending in the ordered review.

row.requirement: Lemma 10.11(ii): zero endpoint-path integrals and closed periods.
reviewed_claims: For every finite p>1, every complex source in the unchanged common W, every signed index and every original isolating disk, the quotient has zero improper integral along every admissible endpoint path that is C1 on its open parameter interval, and along every finite piecewise interior-C1 such path.

The integrals are actual truncated parameter integrals. Their two endpoint truncation parameters approach independently, and existence of the zero limit is proved. Interior corner vertices avoid all gaps; loops, self-intersections and singular endpoint parametrizations are allowed.

A primitive on the entire original cut disk has a common full relative limit at its two endpoints. Noncollapsed complex gaps use inverse-square-root endpoint bounds and opposite cosine-sheet coefficients. Collapsed gaps use a compatible analytic extension of the primitive.

Every finite piecewise C1 closed contour in the original cut disk has zero actual integral, without a prescribed winding number or homotopy. Compact smooth pieces supply integrability. Every original boundary circle also has zero integral on the same W.
For paths C1 up to their endpoints whose full curve integral is integrable, the improper definition agrees with that ordinary curve integral and it is zero.
row.qualification: The path-integral assertion uses the usual piecewise C1 interpretation of contour integration, with the stronger allowance of C1 only on piece interiors. Mere continuous admissibility alone is not presented as an ordinary-integrability theorem. The independently truncated improper limit needs no full-path absolute-integrability premise. The closed-contour result applies off the selected gap, as required for the original quotient. The separate proof displays are still compared in their own ordered rows.

row.requirement: Collapsed-factor cancellation proof.
reviewed_claims: On the unchanged W, a zero gap places its critical point at its periodic midpoint, at every signed index including the central block.
The collapsed standard root is exactly midpoint minus z. Off the selected gap its critical numerator is the same nonzero linear factor, so the selected factor cancels to one.
The quotient is therefore -i times the literal unconditional product over m different from n. The omitted quotient is analytic on the full omitted domain, including the entire original selected disk.

row.requirement: Real-locus period calculation via side deformation and arcosh.
reviewed_claims: The indexed period is analytic on the unchanged common W and is represented locally on the entire original source neighborhood by the original fixed boundary circle.

For every signed integer index, the real half-discriminant is exactly (-1)^n Re(Delta)/2. It equals one at both actual endpoints and is greater than one in an open gap interior, giving the printed signed-discriminant bound.

The new literal kernel is (-1)^(n+1) Delta prime divided by the positive real square root of Re(Delta)^2-4. It equals the lower canonical boundary quotient and the negative upper quotient on the open gap.
The literal kernel is interval-integrable across both actual endpoints. The proof covers collapsed gaps, where the integration interval is degenerate.

Twice the integral from the left endpoint to any point x of the closed gap equals -2 arcosh((-1)^n Re(Delta(x))/2). Thus the coefficient and parity sign are fixed before the full-gap endpoint values vanish.

The existing shrinking contour is clockwise: upper left-to-right minus right endpoint arc minus lower left-to-right minus left endpoint arc. Real upper and lower limiting integrals vanish, as do the endpoint arcs; isolated-circle transport retains the original real-centered circle.

Two public examples exercise a strictly negative interior partial integral at index -1 and p=3/2, and the literal positive-circle formula on an arbitrary original central disk without an open-gap hypothesis.
row.qualification: The printed parity and coefficient -2 match. The direct literal partial-integral identity is new; the full original-circle chain reuses existing period vanishing. Upper and lower mean positive and negative imaginary transverse coordinates after applying the complex half-gap, so rotated and vertical gaps are included. Existing common-domain boundary data supplies isolation, omitted-product analyticity and nonzero interior traces.

The new general cosine-integral theorem uses a single-valued primitive, a continuous square root of the endpoint polynomial and a left endpoint limit. Opposite angles have the same spectral point and opposite nonzero root coefficients. Continuity identifies the regular angle-primitive endpoint values, and real FTC gives a zero full cosine integral. The new literal kernel is the complex half-gap Jacobian times the discriminant derivative divided by the full canonical-root upper or lower boundary value. Collapsed gaps are handled separately: the affine kernels have zero Jacobian, giving the totalized zero-length integral convention; no distinct sides or nonzero boundary traces are asserted there. The existing endpoint-path theorems use actual truncated path integrals with independently tending start and end parameters. They apply on the whole original disk to every interior C1 admissible path and every finite piecewise interior C1 chain, including corners, loops and self-intersections. Primitive differences telescope and the common endpoint limit makes the integral zero. No absolute integrability is needed for this improper statement; the ordinary curve-integral version retains its integrability hypothesis.

This primitive route proves the final admissible-path conclusion without requiring a chosen deformation. All signed indices, finite p>1, original disks and the unchanged common W are retained. The second new example checks the literal original-circle upper-side formula and endpoint integrability at p=3/2 and n=-1, without real-type or open-gap assumptions.

The original-circle equality reuses zero periods, and the final arbitrary-path conclusion follows from full relative primitive limits instead of a new general contour-deformation theorem.
