reviewed_claims: The new maximum theorem bounds the raw coordinate by 2*pi*c*C times the attained maximum of |sigma_m-lambda| on the actual complex gap. It uses the admissible original circle, an unused root filled inside its own disk, and a uniform single-quotient bound on the selected disk.

The maximum of the distance from the actual midpoint is exactly half the gap norm, attained at an endpoint even for a complex or collapsed gap. The root distance is then bounded by the input displacement, midpoint displacement and gap displacement sequences.

Compact single-coordinate replacement supplies one local quotient bound before all omitted indices. The positive sum of three coefficient-magnitude sequences gives a single lp majorant for all F_m^n at a common full root input, with deletion of n before evaluation.

The printed supremum over n different from m is constructed literally as an sSup, not replaced by separate norm bounds. Each supremum is nonnegative and bounded by the same coefficient majorant. Coordinate domination puts the resulting supremum sequence in lp with one locally bounded norm.

Local boundedness and scalar coordinate analyticity give an actual lp-valued Banach power series. The source-first literal-index equation retains the original W, all root inputs and the identical local bound chosen before every omitted index.
row.qualification: Matched with an explicit common ambient lp input when comparing different deleted spaces. Both the actual coordinatewise supremum and the gap maximum are retained; the raw contour normalization is 2*pi. The admissibility clarification in Lemma 12.3 remains in force.

row.requirement: Reality of the scalar equation for real sources and root inputs.
reviewed_claims: For real-type sources, the standard root obeys Schwarz reflection off its real gap, hence is real on the real axis there. With real numerator roots, the single quotient has zero imaginary part on the real selected gap. The printed single auxiliary product is its negative, so its sign does not change this reality statement.

The source reciprocal formula is used only where its unused-root denominator is nonzero. The earlier positive root completion can choose that unused root in its own real disk. The actual equation reality proof covers all real lp root inputs by reflection of the original contour, with no blanket root-placement requirement.

The entire numerator commutes with conjugation, while the canonical root changes sign because its normalization contains 2i. Thus the integrand is anti-conjugate. Reflection reverses the orientation of the real-centered original circle, cancelling that sign and making the raw contour integral real. The real signed n-m factor preserves reality.

The new literal-index theorem transports this conclusion through zero extension and restriction. Every real retained input extends to real full coefficients, including zero at the omitted index. The actual source-first output coordinates therefore have zero imaginary part on the whole original real locus.
row.qualification: Matched for arbitrary real retained lp inputs and every real-type source in the original W. The proof retains the source signs and raw contour normalization; no new root-placement restriction or refutation is introduced.

row.requirement: Original real domain Omega, admissible root placement and the bounded Jacobian matrix.
reviewed_claims: The full original root-placement domain specifies every root before any omitted index. Its restriction to the actual real source Banach space and real lp space is open: finitely many root coordinates have individual margins, while coefficient decay and the original pi/4 tail disks give one pi/8 margin for all remaining coordinates.

The bounded operator is the Frechet root derivative of the original analytic equation. Every matrix coefficient is its coordinate-vector evaluation and the scalar derivative along the corresponding root line. Boundedness and convergence of finite lp truncations give the convergent infinite-matrix representation.

The derivative on literal retained-index lp is conjugate by the exact index isometry. Its operator norm and each retained matrix coefficient equal those of the closed zero-coordinate realization. Neither transport changes the original source domain.
row.qualification: The open real domain, actual bounded derivative and matrix representation match, with direct interfaces on the literal deleted-index spaces.

row.requirement: Lemma 12.5: real nonzero diagonals and uniform diagonal/off-diagonal asymptotics.
reviewed_claims: Every actual matrix entry is real on the full real source/root domain, by differentiating real coordinate lines. Every retained diagonal is nonzero.

The diagonal is exactly 2 plus a reciprocal-index-distance error and an lp sequence. A single neighborhood and nonnegative constants precede every omitted index. Both error bounds retain their 2*pi scaling from the raw contour normalization.

For off-diagonal entries, one lp sequence is the actual weighted row supremum over all equation indices and all distinct columns. Its norm is locally bounded; division by the nonzero integer distance yields the printed reciprocal-distance form.

The two bounds are assembled on a common open neighborhood of the full real source/root pair. Their constants are combined by addition, preserving nonnegativity and uniformity before the omitted index. The original source neighborhood remains open, connected and contains every real source.
row.qualification: The Lemma 12.5 statement matches with the original real-domain topology, exact leading diagonal 2 and simultaneous uniform bounds.

row.requirement: Derivative of the literal complementary product and off-diagonal contour formula.
reviewed_claims: Moving a retained root gives an exact affine formula for the single quotient and then for the literal double-omitted zeta. Filling the unused coordinate at lambda+1 proves the formula even if lambda coincides with the original unused numerator root.

The derivative is precisely zeta/(sigma_r-lambda) where that moved-root denominator is nonzero and lambda lies in the natural omitted-m spectral domain. The two omitted root coordinates are excluded from the variation.

Original root placement makes each moved root avoid the original contour. The finite-product variation passes to the entire-product limit, and continuous contour kernels justify the exact affine integral formula. Uniqueness identifies it with the actual bounded Jacobian coefficient.
The resulting integrand is (sigma_m-lambda)/(sigma_r-lambda) times (n-m)*zeta/w_m. Factoring the constant n-m recovers the printed off-diagonal contour formula, with its original sign.
row.qualification: The retained-root derivative and off-diagonal contour formula match; the direct zeta derivative includes collisions with the unused numerator root.

row.requirement: Off-diagonal inverse-spacing bound and diagonal contour formula.
reviewed_claims: Weighted original-disk separation bounds the denominator on the selected gap. Lemma 12.3 and the uniform weighted-zeta bound give 2*pi*c*L times the sum of the root, midpoint and gap displacement norms for the weighted off-diagonal coefficient.

The three displacement sequences have common local lp norm bounds. Their scaled magnitude sum is a single majorant before both equation index and column. Taking the literal coordinate supremum preserves lp membership and that norm bound, including all finite-head coordinates.

For a diagonal entry, the own root lies strictly inside the selected disk and avoids its circle. Its numerator/denominator factor cancels on that circle, leaving exactly the raw integral of (n-m)*zeta/w_m.
row.qualification: The inverse-spacing estimate and diagonal contour identity match, with the raw 2*pi normalization explicit and a common majorant for all omitted indices and columns.

row.requirement: Diagonal mean-value asymptotic and nonvanishing via root placement.
reviewed_claims: The rotated weighted zeta is analytic near the selected disk and real on its real gap. Lemma 12.3 supplies an actual point mu in G_m and the exact identity Q_mm=-2*pi*i*(n-m)*zeta(mu), also when the gap collapses.

Inserting the decomposition (2.26) gives the exact leading value (-2*pi*i)*(i/pi)=2. The reciprocal and lp error bounds each multiply by 2*pi, and evaluating them at the mean-value points preserves their common disk majorants.

On the natural omitted-m spectral domain, zeta vanishes exactly at retained numerator roots. Absolute summability of the factor errors proves a nonzero product when all retained factors are nonzero; a retained zero factor gives the converse.
Root placement separates all retained roots from the selected G_m. Thus zeta(mu) is nonzero at the actual mean-value point, and the other scalar factors are nonzero for m unequal to n.
row.qualification: The positive nonvanishing argument uses G_m, which contains the mean-value point mu. This replaces the printed concluding gap reference G_n with the selected-gap statement needed by the proof; the diagonal identity and constants are retained.

row.requirement: Lemma 12.6: invertible diagonal plus compact remainder.
reviewed_claims: At each point of the original open real root-placement domain and for every omitted index, the actual bounded Jacobian is a diagonal continuous linear equivalence plus a compact operator. The original source neighborhood and all preceding Lemma 12.5 data are retained.

The diagonal and its inverse have exact coordinate formulas: multiply by the actual diagonal matrix entry and its reciprocal, respectively. The compact part is the canonical subtraction of that diagonal from the original bounded Jacobian.

Conjugating by the exact deleted-index equivalence gives the same decomposition on the literal retained-index spaces. Compactness is preserved by the two bounded compositions, and restriction/zero extension preserves both coordinate formulas.
row.qualification: The original-domain diagonal-plus-compact statement matches, including an explicit inverse on the literal retained-index spaces.

row.requirement: Diagonal tail limit two, explicit inverse and off-diagonal matrix remainder.
reviewed_claims: For each fixed omitted index, the reciprocal-distance error tends to zero as the row index escapes on either signed tail. The lp error also tends to zero. Their sum gives an actual epsilon cutoff and the filter limit of the diagonal entries to 2.

The tail is bounded away from zero. Taking a positive minimum with the finitely many nonzero retained head values gives one strictly positive lower bound on all retained diagonal entries. The bounded reciprocal symbol defines the actual continuous inverse.

The diagonal symbol is bounded by the norm of the actual operator. Subtraction gives a bounded remainder with zero diagonal and unchanged off-diagonal entries; deleted row and column coefficients vanish. Thus the Lemma 12.5 reciprocal estimates apply to its actual matrix.
row.qualification: The two-sided diagonal limit is for fixed n, exactly as needed by Lemma 12.6. The inverse includes every retained finite-head entry and the remainder is the actual operator subtraction.

row.requirement: Mixed row-sum estimate and finite-rank norm approximation proving compactness.
reviewed_claims: The literal mixed row-power expression is summable. A reciprocal majorant constructs each actual matrix row in the finite conjugate lp space; its norm is bounded by the output majorant times the norm of the translated punctured reciprocal lattice. Raising that norm to p gives exactly the displayed inner q-power sum raised to p/q, and a common lp majorant controls the outer sum.

For 1<p<infinity the conjugate exponent also lies strictly between 1 and infinity. The generic mixed-power proof applies to the actual off-diagonal Jacobian, including its zero deleted row and column. The source schematic lp and l1 terms are represented by positive summable majorants.

Hölder duality and convergence of finite matrix sums identify every output coordinate with its actual conjugate-space row pairing. A single lp row majorant therefore bounds the entire operator on all inputs.

The actual finite output cutoffs have finite-dimensional range. Their operator-norm error is bounded by the lp tail norm of the common row majorant, which tends to zero. Hence the remainder is compact.

The same finite cutoffs, conjugated to literal retained indices, still have finite-dimensional range and converge in operator norm. Their exact coordinate formula keeps a retained index precisely when it belongs to the finite set; including the omitted integer in that set has no effect.
row.qualification: The mixed double-power summability and uniform finite-rank approximation match for the actual matrix and operator, with direct literal-index interfaces.

row.requirement: Lemma 12.7: injectivity of the deleted-space Jacobian.
reviewed_claims: At every original real root-placement point and every omitted index, the actual bounded root Jacobian is injective for every finite exponent strictly above one. The same open connected source neighborhood and all preceding decomposition data are retained.
The proof covers complex kernel vectors: real matrix entries send their real and imaginary parts to zero separately; the real gap-zero argument then kills both parts.
The literal retained-index derivative is exactly conjugate to the original derivative by the deleted-index isometry. Its injectivity therefore preserves the full original root input before omission.
row.qualification: The original-domain injectivity statement matches, with a direct interface on the literal retained-index space.

row.requirement: Kernel derivative numerator is entire and has zero off-diagonal periods.
reviewed_claims: Joint analyticity of the actual entire candidate makes its root-direction derivative entire in the spectral parameter. It equals the derivative along the full coefficient line, with the omitted direction coordinate zero.

Every actual Jacobian row has its unconditional sum against a deleted coefficient vector. Differentiation of the original contour functional gives exactly the signed factor n-m times the contour integral of the entire variation divided by the canonical root.
A zero kernel output and m different from n cancel the nonzero signed factor. Thus the entire variation has zero period on every retained original contour.
row.qualification: The entire numerator and its zero-period identity match the displayed kernel equation, including its normalization.

row.requirement: Real gap zeros and exterior-circle logarithmic derivative expansion.
reviewed_claims: For real source roots and a real direction, the entire variation is real on the real axis. The local-numerator form of Lemma 12.2 then supplies a zero in every retained real gap, including a collapsed gap. Its analyticity requirement holds because this numerator is entire.

Original isolating disks are disjoint. A finite-head radius and the common small tail disks give one cutoff after which every half-integer-radius circle avoids every original disk and every original root.

The logarithmic derivative identity is proved first for the literal finite product. Locally uniform convergence of the analytic coefficient-line products gives convergence of their derivatives. Absolute summability of the actual-root resolvent identifies its symmetric cutoff limit and yields the displayed infinite identity.
Real and imaginary kernel splitting supplies the real-direction hypothesis before using the gap-zero argument.
row.qualification: Gap zeros and the actual product-variation identity match; reality is justified before the gap argument.

row.requirement: Sine product identity for the entire interpolation numerator.
reviewed_claims: The exact identity is f_n(z)*(sigma_n-z)/(2*sin(z)) equal to the relative product over all integer roots. The minus sign in the full free product -2*sin(z) cancels the candidate normalization.
Multiplying the actual root-resolvent identity by the omitted-root factor gives exactly the printed variation quotient. The omitted direction term is zero, so the full sum is the retained sum.
row.qualification: The displayed sine identity matches without any sign or constant correction. Later individual-product asymptotics are a separate comparison.

row.requirement: Exterior product asymptotic, Holder tail estimate, interpolation and vanishing of the kernel vector.
reviewed_claims: The relative product tends to one uniformly on the full expanding circles. A positive Holder split bounds the free resolvent by the coefficient tail norm plus the finite inverse-denominator q-power sum, where q is the finite conjugate exponent.
For the cutoff |m|<=floor(nu/2), every free denominator on the circle is at least pi*(nu+1)/2 and the number of terms is at most nu+1. The finite q-norm is therefore at most (2/pi)*(nu+1)^(1/q-1).

One exterior threshold gives the actual-root denominator comparison with factor two. With lattice separation pi/4, the actual absolute resolvent sum is at most (8*C_p/pi)*norm(h-truncate(h))+(4/pi)*norm(h)*(nu+1)^(1/q-1). Both terms tend to zero. The threshold is independent of the direction and cutoff, and the bound holds around each entire sufficiently large circle.

Gap sample displacements lie in lp by the endpoint displacement and gap-length majorants. Inserting the unused root is a finite coordinate change. Disjoint original disks make these interpolation roots distinct, giving an entire product with exactly those simple zeros.

The ratio of the two root products is bounded by four outside one threshold. Together with the arbitrarily small actual-root resolvent this bounds the interpolation quotient. Filling its simple common zeros gives an entire quotient; the maximum-modulus argument on expanding circles forces the numerator to vanish. Continuity removes the unused root factor.

At a retained simple original root the entire variation equals minus the direction coordinate times the nonzero spectral derivative. Its vanishing therefore recovers every coefficient, completing the real and then complex kernel argument.
row.qualification: The printed signed-distance and finite-head estimates are replaced by the explicit uniform radial bound above. The product asymptotic, interpolation and injectivity conclusions are preserved. This is a positive correction; no new refutation is added.

row.requirement: Corollary 12.8: Fredholm alternative gives a bounded linear isomorphism.
reviewed_claims: The original diagonal-plus-compact decomposition is reduced to D*(1-T), with T=-D inverse composed with the compact remainder. Injectivity excludes eigenvalue one; the compact-operator Fredholm alternative supplies surjectivity.

The Banach inverse theorem gives a continuous inverse to the actual complex Jacobian. Conjugation commutes with the real-entry operator and hence its inverse, so real inputs have real inverse images. Restriction gives a continuous real equivalence exactly equal to the actual real derivative, compatible with complex inclusion.

Conjugating the complex equivalence by the deleted-index isometry gives a continuous linear equivalence exactly equal to the derivative on the literal retained-index spaces. The source neighborhood, full real root input and original root-placement domain remain unchanged.
row.qualification: Both the real and complex isomorphisms match. The inverse bound is at each fixed source point and omitted index; no uniform-in-index bound is asserted.

row.requirement: Proposition 12.9: unique global real analytic solution and real gap placement.
reviewed_claims: For every finite p strictly above one and every omitted index, the actual equation has a unique global real analytic solution on the real source Banach space. The same open connected complex neighborhood and preceding Jacobian isomorphism data are retained.

The solution predicate includes the actual sequence equation and membership in an original deleted placement domain. The canonical graph lies in every supplied original disk family over its admissible real sources, and every retained root lies in its actual periodic gap.

The real deleted coefficient space embeds exactly into the complex deleted space. Its placement domain is the projection of the original full real domain, with the missing coordinate filled by the real center of its assigned disk.
row.qualification: The global solution, uniqueness, original-domain graph and assigned gap placement match the proposition for all finite p > 1.

row.requirement: Every admissible solution root lies in its assigned gap.
reviewed_claims: The actual real equation zero transports to the complex equation and then to each original scalar period with its nonzero n-m factor.
For an open real gap, the real mean-value contour formula gives a numerator zero in that gap. At a collapsed gap, the Cauchy formula gives the same conclusion.

The entire candidate has exactly its retained displaced roots as zeros. The assigned disjoint disks identify the gap zero with the correspondingly indexed root, so originally placed solutions satisfy all retained gap conditions.
row.qualification: Gap placement matches, including collapsed gaps. The exact product zero set and disjoint placement make the root identification explicit.

row.requirement: Local implicit solution and the continuation setup.
reviewed_claims: Joint analyticity of the actual equation and bijectivity of its actual root derivative give a complex analytic local zero branch with its prescribed initial value.

On the real source submodule, the canonical real analytic solution and pointwise uniqueness provide a branch through every originally placed real solution. The branch graph remains in the same original domain near its base point.

The new literal retained-index interface transports the branch through the exact coefficient isometry. It preserves the full original root input before omission, the initial value and the actual sequence equation zero on a neighborhood.
row.qualification: The local implicit extension matches; the public retained-index theorem exposes the same branch in the source indexing convention.

row.requirement: Limit of source/root sequences, gap compactness and global continuation on the simply connected real locus.
reviewed_claims: The actual periodic endpoints vary continuously along converging real sources. Their locally uniform lp tails bound the tails of every gap-contained root choice, with a common bound for all omitted indices. Finite-rank truncation compactness yields a strongly convergent lp subsequence.

Continuous endpoints retain the limiting gap placement. Contour invariance transfers the varying admissible contour equations to one fixed local chart before continuity passes the zero equation to the limit.

Solvability is nonempty and relatively open and closed in the connected real source locus. The set of sources admitting two distinct solutions is also relatively open and closed: if two limiting roots coincide, local uniqueness in their common chart forces the nearby roots to coincide. Free-source uniqueness therefore gives global pointwise uniqueness.

Local complex analytic implicit branches restrict to a globally real analytic canonical solution. Every sequence of originally placed solutions over convergent sources then converges in the full real lp norm by pointwise uniqueness and continuity of this map.
row.qualification: The continuation and global uniqueness conclusions match. The implementation supplies strong lp compactness explicitly and uses clopen solvability and multiplicity instead of a separate monodromy argument. The real Banach source space is also simply connected, as checked through the pinned mathlib instance.

row.requirement: Free source solution and uniqueness from collapsed free gaps.
reviewed_claims: At the free source, the actual selected contour equation at the zero coefficient sequence vanishes by its exact Cauchy and orthogonality formula.

Every free periodic gap is the singleton containing its free center. Assigned placement and the exact numerator zero set force all retained coefficients of any solution to vanish, even for complex root inputs.
The canonical original real solution consequently has value zero at the free source, fixing the unique global analytic map.
row.qualification: The free solution and its uniqueness match, with their normalization and collapsed-gap argument retained.

row.requirement: Lemma 12.10: extension of every branch to one common complex source neighborhood with original root placement.
reviewed_claims: All actual Proposition 12.9 root maps extend to one open simply connected complex neighborhood containing the entire real source locus and lying inside the unchanged preceding source domain. The domain is chosen before every omitted index.

Each extension solves the actual original sequence equation and agrees exactly with its canonical real solution. The new literal retained-index interfaces preserve these properties by the exact coefficient isometry.

Uniform analytic equation and inverse bounds give common positive branch radii. Branches agree on overlapping real-centered balls by real agreement and the complex identity principle. The atlas domain contracts to its real projection and then to zero, proving simple connectivity.

Compactness of the real gap-root product gives a margin inside any supplied original disk family. Uniform branch stability then puts all retained roots into those same disks on one smaller source ball, independently of both indices. Restricting the source neighborhood preserves the disks and their comparison constant.
row.qualification: The common extension and root-placement statement match. Supplied disks are retained while their source neighborhood may be restricted, as made explicit by original_assignment. The later printed inverse-bound proof passages retain their own pending comparison status.

row.requirement: Jacobian contour formula and exact multiplier expansion (2.28).
reviewed_claims: The actual original Jacobian entry is the contour integral of the retained root ratio times (n-m), the double-omitted auxiliary factor and the reciprocal selected standard root. Original disk placement supplies contour avoidance for every retained input direction.

The double-omitted factor is (1/i)/(sigma_n-z) times the negative single auxiliary product from (2.25). Rewriting pi*(n-m)/(sigma_n-z) therefore gives exactly the printed factor 1/(i*pi), with no change of sign or normalization.

The literal multiplier equals one plus ((n*pi-sigma_n)+(z-m*pi))/(sigma_n-z). Uniform lattice bounds and original disk separation bound its error by K/abs(n-m), with K independent of the indices, root input and point in the original row disk.
For each fixed row and every positive tolerance, one tail cutoff works for all root inputs placed in the original disks and all points of that disk, as the omitted index escapes in either direction.
row.qualification: The contour identity and (2.28) match with their exact constants. The opening uniform-inverse sentence announces the later argument; its detailed estimates are compared in subsequent groups.

row.requirement: Limiting all-index matrix Q-star and its diagonal/off-diagonal estimates (2.29).
reviewed_claims: For each fixed row and column, the actual Jacobian entries converge to the literal Q-star contour entry in both directions of the omitted index. Deleted-coordinate norm convergence, joint quotient continuity and uniform rational-multiplier convergence justify passing the limit through each compact contour.

The limiting integral is defined for every pair of integer indices. The intrinsic operator has those entries on every supplied original circle; uniqueness of coordinate limits makes the definition independent of contour choices.

On the original real placed-root domain, each diagonal entry is twice the single analytic quotient at an actual point in the corresponding gap. Disjoint original disks make this value nonzero, including collapsed gaps, and a locally bounded lp quotient-error sequence gives the exact form 2 plus lp.

Multiplying an off-diagonal entry by its signed index difference gives the actual original equation coordinate divided by pi. A common lp equation majorant therefore bounds all columns in each row by B_m/abs(m-r). The local bounds use the original joint root/source topology.
row.qualification: The scalar limit and both parts of (2.29) match. The negative single auxiliary product accounts for the printed contour sign; the diagonal leading value stays 2. Scalar convergence alone is not used to assert operator-norm convergence.

row.requirement: Bounded full-space operator and diagonal-two extension of deleted Jacobians.
reviewed_claims: A common analytic chart gives an eventual bound on the norms of the full Jacobians. Their basis-entry limits define a bounded operator by taking finite linear combinations, using lp lower semicontinuity and extending from dense finite-support inputs. The constructed operator has exactly the contour matrix.

Real original inputs give real matrix entries. Conjugation equivariance extends this to all real coefficient vectors. The new bounded operator on real lp has complex inclusion exactly equal to the intrinsic complex limiting operator, with no loss of matrix information.

Every deleted Jacobian extends to the full lp space by placing 2 on its omitted diagonal and zero in the remaining entries of that row and column. Its retained block is the actual original derivative, identified with every valid selected-contour derivative.

The operator-norm convergence announced at the end of the passage holds at each fixed original real placed-root input in both index directions. Its existing proof combines the diagonal and off-diagonal norm limits. The later detailed estimates and local-uniformity quantifiers are left to their own ordered groups.
row.qualification: The bounded real operator and diagonal-two extensions match. The announced norm-limit theorem is reused with its fixed-input scope; this group does not claim convergence uniformly on one fixed ambient neighborhood.

row.requirement: Exact diagonal norm split and the moving omitted-coordinate term.
reviewed_claims: For every coefficient vector, the p-th power of the actual diagonal difference norm is exactly the omitted-coordinate contribution plus the sum of retained-coordinate contributions. The full Jacobian has value 2 on the omitted diagonal, and every retained diagonal is its original contour derivative.

The retained entry difference is exactly (i/pi) times the original contour of (indexRatio-1) times the analytic single quotient over the selected standard root. The literal single auxiliary product is the negative of this quotient, so this has the printed 1/(i*pi) normalization.

One S in lp satisfies Q-star_mm=2+S_m. The moving term is bounded by |S_n| times the input norm, with constant one, uniformly over every index and input vector. Thus its p-th power has one summable scalar coefficient, as required by the printed ell-one notation.
row.qualification: The diagonal split and moving-coordinate estimate match, including the exact normalization and leading value 2. Bounds refer to the actual original operators; roots are real and placed in the original disks where the lp diagonal description is invoked.

row.requirement: Separate contour-error bounds with explicit local constants.
reviewed_claims: Original disk separation bounds the multiplier error on the actual row gap by c*(|a_n|+|M_m|+|G_m|)/|n-m|, where M is the midpoint displacement and G the gap sequence. It also gives analyticity on the filled row disk, and the standard-root quotient is integrable on its enclosing circle.

Lemma 12.3 gives the explicit factor 2 for the period normalized by i/pi, for complex analytic numerators and also collapsed gaps. If the single quotient is bounded by L, the two normalized contour terms are bounded respectively by 2*c*L*|a_n|/|n-m| and 2*c*L*(|M_m|+|G_m|)/|n-m|.

One joint neighborhood of the root and source and one constant are chosen before both integer indices. A quotient-error majorant with norm at most Cq gives the common constant 2*c*(Cq+1). The root and spectral displacement sequences remain explicit in the bound.
row.qualification: The local big-O statements match with positive explicit constants, retaining the denominator also for the first term. Locality is in the printed joint root/source domain. The common quotient bound does not assert uniformly vanishing lp tails on one fixed neighborhood.

row.requirement: Diagonal operator-norm convergence from a corrected output-index tail estimate.
reviewed_claims: For n nonzero and 2*K<=|n|, a reciprocal column with omitted coordinate zero has norm at most (2/|n|)*norm(b)+norm(b-truncate_K(b)). Here truncate_K cuts off the output indices outside [-K,K]. The constants are 2 on the finite head and 1 on the tail. A single-coordinate application makes the same estimate uniform over the output index.

For the actual diagonal operators, one C>=0 and one S in lp with Q-star_mm=2+S_m give norm(Dn-Dstar)<=|S_n|+C*(|a_n|+(2/|n|)*(norm(M)+norm(G))+norm(M-truncate_K(M))+norm(G-truncate_K(G))). C and S precede n and K in the quantifiers.

Use the output-index tails |m|>K, with 2*K<=|n|, in place of the printed |m-n|>=|n|/2 tail. First make the two lp tails small and then increase |n|. The moving lp coefficients and the reciprocal finite head also tend to zero, yielding the claimed diagonal operator-norm limit.

The separate convergence interface uses the actual fixed-row limits and one uniform diagonal tail. The supporting proof controls deleted-root variation by a common analytic Lipschitz estimate, handles both open and collapsed real gaps, and gives convergence as the omitted index escapes in either direction.
row.qualification: The convergence conclusion is retained with the positive corrected output-index tail bound and explicit head/tail constants. The original real placed-root domain is used; no gap-containment restriction is added. This step adds no refutation and makes no stronger fixed-neighborhood uniform-convergence claim.

row.requirement: Exact off-diagonal split into the omitted row and retained rows.
reviewed_claims: The off-diagonal part K-n of the full original Jacobian has zero omitted output row. For every input h, the p-th power of norm((K-star-K-n)h) is exactly |(K-star h)_n|^p plus the sum over retained output rows.
The equality is for the actual bounded original operators and all signed omitted indices; no matrix estimate is substituted for the operator itself.
row.qualification: The norm decomposition matches exactly. Its algebraic form also holds for complex inputs, with finite 1<p<infinity.

row.requirement: Positive Holder estimate for the distinguished row.
reviewed_claims: For conjugate exponents p and q, one B_r in lp is chosen before n and h, and |(K-star h)_n| <= |B_r_n|*Cq*norm(h), where Cq is the norm in lq of the punctured reciprocal integer lattice.
The proof bounds the absolute row kernel in lq and applies Holder to its dual pairing with h. Raising to p yields a summable coefficient |B_r_n|^p*Cq^p, which tends to zero as |n| grows.
row.qualification: Use this positive absolute-kernel estimate in place of the printed factorization through a signed reciprocal sum. The distinguished-row decay conclusion is retained; no refutation is added.

row.requirement: Exact retained-row split and explicit power-triangle constant.
reviewed_claims: The omitted input column of K-n also vanishes. Deleting output coordinate n splits (K-star-K-n)h exactly into the error applied to the retained input and the omitted-input column of K-star.
The p-th power of the retained-output norm is at most 2^(p-1) times the sum of the p-th powers of these two actual terms. This supplies an explicit constant for the printed implicit inequality I+II.

The normalized original contour differences identify the retained-input term. The unit complex phase in the printed I numerator does not change its absolute p-th power; the exact operator contour normalization is kept.
row.qualification: The two-term split and implicit inequality match. The explicit positive factor is 2^(p-1); no claim that the printed implicit constant is incorrect is needed.

row.requirement: Distinguished-column norm bound with vanishing output tails.
reviewed_claims: One B_c in lp bounds every column. For n nonzero and 2*K<=|n|, norm(K-star(single_n 1)) <= (2/|n|)*norm(B_c)+norm(B_c-truncate_K(B_c)), where truncate_K keeps output indices in [-K,K].
For arbitrary h, the same right-hand side times norm(h) bounds K-star(single_n h_n), with no extra constant. Output-coordinate deletion is a contraction, so its p-th power bounds term II.
First choose K to make the actual lp output tail small, then increase |n| to control the finite head. The head and tail factors are 2 and 1.
row.qualification: Use the column lp norm and output-index tail in place of the printed supremum and moving-difference cutoff. This positive replacement preserves the vanishing of term II for the original placed roots, including complex roots at a real-type source.

row.requirement: Double inverse-spacing contour bound and retained-operator tail estimate.
reviewed_claims: Every retained off-diagonal difference is the original (i/pi)-normalized contour of (indexRatio-1)*(sigma_m-z)*q_m(z)/(sigma_k-z), divided by the standard root. The literal auxiliary product is -q_m, retaining the source normalization.

Every actual normalized integral agrees with such a representative modulo an integer multiple of pi. The representatives and the actual chosen integral are real at real-type sources.

reviewed_claims: Theta_n is exactly eta_n plus the absolutely convergent beta correction. Changing the normalized eta integral changes theta by an integer multiple of 2*pi.

row.requirement: Corollary 13.2: action-action brackets vanish on the full real locus.

Action variations are contour integrals of regular discriminant variations. Discriminant commutation and bilinear contour integration give zero action-action pairing for all signed n,m and all real-type sources at every finite p greater than one.

The pairing is the absolutely convergent Fourier sum with reversed frequency and sign -i. Its square-summable coefficient witness is uniquely determined by the cotangent. Neither action gap is required to be open.

Both selected angle gaps must be open, exactly excluding Z_n union Z_m. The statement applies to every signed index pair and every finite p greater than one.
row.qualification: The angle-angle identity matches with precisely its two open-gap hypotheses. The earlier physical NLS Dirichlet-motion obligation in Section 7 is not declared resolved by this spectral bracket comparison.

Below two, action and angle differential compatibility preserves the complete regular coefficient pairs and their Fourier pairing. The same identity therefore holds for all finite p greater than one.
