row.qualification: Above and below the Hilbert exponent the realization and restriction arguments retain the same physical coefficients.

row.requirement: The two G.7 estimates used in Lemma 16.1.
reviewed_claims: The actual midpoint derivatives form an outer lp sequence, and the actual Dirichlet derivatives differ from the free half-sum functional by an outer lp sequence.

The H1 realization supplies the required hypothesis. Independent Hilbert estimates with the requested outer exponent, followed by bounded restriction, cover p<2. Bounded conjugate-gradient recovery gives the physical pair norms.
row.qualification: The free modes are those displayed in Section 16. Earlier qualifications on literal Appendix G displays remain in their own comparison records.

row.requirement: Anti-discriminant samples and the moving-root derivative term.
reviewed_claims: Both delta(mu_n) and its spectral derivative at the actual Dirichlet roots belong to lp. A common source neighborhood and cutoff give a tail majorant, and finite modification retains all central samples.

The Dirichlet derivative error is lp and its free functional has a common bound, so the full Dirichlet derivatives are uniformly bounded in n. Multiplication by the lp spectral derivative therefore gives an lp sequence of moving-root cotangents.
row.qualification: This conclusion holds with the actual roots and source norm. It does not require an estimate uniform over an arbitrary source norm ball.

row.requirement: The G.6 anti-discriminant gradient error.
reviewed_claims: At the actual Dirichlet roots, subtracting the free anti-discriminant cotangent gives an outer lp sequence. Multiplication by i identifies the displayed signed cosine times the physical mode difference.
Physical H1 estimates cover p>=2, and exact derivative restriction from independently summable Hilbert cotangents covers 1<p<2.
row.qualification: The spectral variable is held fixed for this cotangent. The separate moving-root contribution is retained in S16-010 and equation (3.3).

row.requirement: Separate own-index product asymptotics and the resulting auxiliary error.
reviewed_claims: Two new positive theorems establish Q_n(mu_n)-1 in lp and psi_n(mu_n)+2*cos(pi*n) in lp for the actual original root family, at every real source and every finite p>1. All signed indices, the central head and collapsed gaps are included; no finite-gap hypothesis is needed.

The shared actual-gap majorant is chosen before both the deleted index and the sampled gap index. Real Dirichlet interlacing permits sampling on the diagonal n=k. Filling the deleted coordinate with its midpoint leaves the deleted numerator unchanged.

The signed omitted product P differs from cos(pi*n) by an lp sequence and is bounded. The exact identity psi=-2*Q*P then gives the second error as -2*((Q-1)*P+(P-cos(pi*n))). This avoids exchanging the quantifiers in the weaker fixed-family estimates.

The needed auxiliary conclusion 2*phi_n+cos(pi*n) in lp is already proved directly as a full Banach-analytic sequence on the unchanged complex W. The original preconnected-domain argument fixes and propagates the omitted-product parity branch.
row.qualification: The positive Q convention from S16-007 is retained. The two separate product estimates are proved for all real sources, a stronger scope than the finite-gap source used here. The full-complex local uniformity and analyticity in the next source sentence concern the auxiliary and are supplied by its separate original-domain theorem. No new refutation is added.

row.requirement: Uniform auxiliary gradients and the delta times gradient term.
reviewed_claims: One original-source neighborhood bounds the complete auxiliary error sequence. Nested-ball Cauchy estimates then bound every actual auxiliary Frechet derivative by C and every physical conjugate gradient by 2*C, uniformly in n.
The lp anti-discriminant samples multiplied by these bounded gradients form an lp sequence. At the real closed gaps used by (3.3) the anti-discriminant sample is exactly zero.
row.qualification: The local bound is valid at every complex point of the original W; the gradient pairing represents the full actual differential.

row.requirement: The auxiliary-weighted anti-discriminant error.
reviewed_claims: The auxiliary is bounded because its signed normalization error is lp. Multiplying it by the G.6 error and the moving-root error therefore preserves lp summability.

The exact closed-cotangent decomposition also retains the auxiliary normalization error multiplied by the bounded free anti-discriminant cotangent. This accounts for the leading signed mode in the next display.
row.qualification: The estimates use bounded scalar/vector products in the actual operator norm and then the bounded physical gradient map; no isometric identification of these two norms is assumed.

row.requirement: Combining the errors and including the finite open-gap head.
reviewed_claims: Outside the finite set of open gaps the actual eta derivative equals the exact closed-gap expression. Its error from the signed free functional is lp by the three preceding estimates.
Finite modification supplies the full sequence, including each open gap. Recovering the physical coefficients gives exactly the two -2 free modes in Lemma 16.1, which feed the rectangular estimate.
row.qualification: The tail equality is simultaneous in all signed indices and sign parameters. All finite p>1 are retained.

row.requirement: Lemma 16.2 for the actual rectangular coordinate gradients.
reviewed_claims: At every real spectral finite-gap source the actual x and y sequence-coordinate gradients differ from their explicit free gradients by outer lp sequences in the full Holder-conjugate pair norm.
The theorem identifies the scalar and actual sequence derivatives on a neighborhood and covers every finite p>1.
row.qualification: No additional Sobolev or open-gap premise is supplied by the caller.

row.requirement: The rectangular formula used in the product rule.
reviewed_claims: The original sequence entries have the sum in x and difference in y, with their exact sqrt(8) and i*sqrt(8) denominators.
The actual rectangular derivatives are the same normalized sum and difference of the signed weighted derivatives.
row.qualification: These identities retain the common Chapter 3 domain and the original root family.

row.requirement: Root error, finite-gap beta decay, vanishing tail and Cauchy bounds.
reviewed_claims: The actual xi-1 sequence is lp at every real source. At a real finite-gap source the beta series has only finitely many nonzero gap-index terms; the reciprocal estimate gives |beta_n|<=K/|n| outside one symmetric cutoff.
Real interlacing makes the eta coordinates zero at every collapsed gap, hence outside a finite set. The product rule there removes both the normalization and beta derivative terms exactly.

Separate Cauchy estimates give uniform-in-n bounds for all three full derivatives and their physical gradients. The root bound holds near each real source; beta and eta bounds hold at every point of their original complex domains.
row.qualification: For each fixed eta sign the neighborhood and constant precede all n; a finite intersection handles both signs. The beta decay is for the fixed finite-gap source, not uniform over an arbitrary neighborhood of finite-gap sources.

row.requirement: The two intermediate rectangular gradient estimates, with y corrected.
reviewed_claims: The new direct theorems prove that dx minus (dz_plus+dz_minus)/sqrt(8), and dy minus (dz_plus-dz_minus)/(i*sqrt(8)), have outer lp source-operator norms.
The original-family interface gives the same estimates for physical Holder-conjugate gradients of actual sequence entries, with all signed indices and the finite open-gap head included.
The proof subtracts the normalized eta free-mode errors from the rectangular free-mode errors. Exact cancellation retains both denominators and the sine orientation.
row.qualification: The printed unscripted z in the second expression is replaced directly by y. Two positive theorems and public examples at p=3/2 and p=4 are added; no refutation is added.

row.requirement: Normalization by the exact free Fourier inverse.
reviewed_claims: A_phi is exactly the bounded free Fourier inverse composed with the actual Jacobian. Its difference from identity equals that inverse composed with the actual Fourier remainder.
row.qualification: The inverse is a bounded linear equivalence for every finite p>1. No general-p isometry is assumed.

row.requirement: Unconditional inverse Fourier reconstruction with the corrected sign.
reviewed_claims: The inverse of two single output modes at -n is a*d_plus_n minus b*d_minus_n. Mapping the unconditional lp coordinate series through the bounded inverse proves the full reconstruction in the original source norm.
row.qualification: The printed positive y-gradient term is replaced by a negative term. Existing historical sign evidence is preserved without adding a new witness.

row.requirement: Equation (3.4) for every complex source and input vector.
reviewed_claims: Substituting the exact coordinate derivatives into the corrected inverse Fourier series gives A_phi h as the sum of dx_{-n}(h)*d_plus_n minus dy_{-n}(h)*d_minus_n.

The series converges unconditionally in the original source norm at every complex point of V and for every complex input vector. The preceding gradient representation gives the physical pairing interpretation.
row.qualification: The corrected negative y term and frequency reversal are retained.

row.requirement: Lemma 16.3: isomorphism equivalence and analytic compact perturbation.
reviewed_claims: Composition with the explicit Fourier equivalence transports bounded linear isomorphisms in both directions between the Jacobian and A_phi.
A_phi varies real analytically on the complete real source space and differs from identity by a compact operator at every real source and every finite p>1.
row.qualification: The isomorphism equivalence is not by itself an invertibility proof; the later Section 17 argument supplies invertibility.

row.requirement: The normalized remainder series.
reviewed_claims: Apply the corrected inverse Fourier series to (d_phi Omega-d_0 Omega)h. The two coefficients are the actual rectangular derivative errors, and the y-gradient basis term carries a minus sign.
row.qualification: The operator equality is exact. The source series is interpreted with the corrected reconstruction sign.

row.requirement: Literal finite-rank gradient-basis cutoffs.
reviewed_claims: The cutoff truncates both actual Fourier-remainder outputs and applies the bounded inverse. Its exact finite sum uses the corrected negative y-gradient term.
The range lies in the span of the reconstructed x and y coordinate modes in the finite index set. Finite dimensionality proves that the operator has finite rank.
row.qualification: Reindexing n to -n identifies the literal symmetric cutoffs in the source. The construction also permits arbitrary finite index sets.

row.requirement: A sufficient original-norm tail bound with its reconstruction constant.
reviewed_claims: The valid operator-norm bound is ||FourierInverse|| times the maximum of the two lp majorant tail norms. These majorants are constructed from the actual rectangular derivative errors at the finite-gap source.

It follows by coordinate/operator norm bounds, the output product norm, and bounded reconstruction into the genuine source p-norm. This supplies the required vanishing estimate without the printed coefficient-to-source isometry equality.
row.qualification: The existing correction retains the necessary multiplicative operator norm. No new proof that the printed equality is wrong is added.

row.requirement: Operator-norm convergence and compactness at every real source.
reviewed_claims: Finite-exponent lp tails tend to zero, so the actual finite-rank cutoffs converge in operator norm at every real finite-gap source, including along the symmetric integer cutoffs.

Finite-gap sources are proved dense in the original source norm. Continuity of the actual Jacobian and closedness of the compact operators extend compactness to all real sources; bounded Fourier inversion gives the statement for A_phi-identity.
row.qualification: Analytic dependence supplies continuity, but density and norm-closedness are the additional ingredients needed for this conclusion.

units.assessment_convention: Current ordered ledger; all historical supporting records retained.

row.requirement: Connection to the remaining properties of Theorem 14.1.
reviewed_claims: The original-family package supplies the remaining local inverse, injectivity and stated surjectivity properties. Its constructor proves the package fields from the actual preceding source construction.
row.qualification: The same normalized family and compatible Chapter 3 domain are retained. Global injectivity holds for every finite p>1; surjectivity is asserted only for p<=2.

row.requirement: Proposition 17.1: local diffeomorphism at every finite exponent above one.
reviewed_claims: At every real source and every finite p>1 the actual real derivative is a bounded linear equivalence. The inverse function theorem gives an analytic local inverse with both inverse identities and the exact strict derivative of the inverse.
The complex extension also has both local inverse identities near each real source.
row.qualification: No invertibility premise is supplied by the caller. The complex local result concerns neighborhoods of real sources, not every complex point of the full construction domain.

row.requirement: Normalized Jacobian equivalence and compact-perturbation Fredholm step.
reviewed_claims: Composition with the exact bounded Fourier inverse identifies invertibility of the actual Jacobian with invertibility of its normalization. The normalized operator is identity plus compact.

The compact spectral decomposition gives the needed Banach-space alternatives: dense range implies bijectivity, and injectivity implies bijectivity. This supplies the role of the printed index-zero Fredholm argument.
row.qualification: The implementation does not require a Hilbert adjoint on a general p-source space. The actual compact-perturbation alternatives retain the full finite exponent range.

row.requirement: Canonical images with consistent swapped x/y labels.
reviewed_claims: For p>=2, the actual x Hamiltonian maps to a positive y output mode, and the y Hamiltonian maps to a negative x output mode.
After exact Fourier normalization these become A K b_x=-d_y and A K b_y=-d_x, with the reflected index -m. Both labels are swapped consistently.
row.qualification: The unswapped printed labels are corrected directly. Hamiltonian source directions here require p>=2; the separate inclusion argument handles smaller exponents. Existing historical refutations are unchanged.

row.requirement: Dense modes and Jacobian invertibility, with the correct dual interpretation.
reviewed_claims: The pairing argument must use the same swapped labels as the corrected canonical images. The proof instead gives actual source preimages for both output modes, then places every finite output truncation in the Jacobian range.

For p>=2 truncation convergence gives dense range and hence bijectivity. For p<2 compatibility transports a kernel vector to the Hilbert Jacobian; its injectivity and injective coefficient inclusion kill the vector. The compact-perturbation alternative gives surjectivity.
row.qualification: The following printed pairing display is not certified merely because it uses an opposite label. The correction is consistent in both displays, and a Holder-conjugate cotangent is not treated as an arbitrary source vector below two.

row.requirement: Proposition 17.2: global injectivity.
reviewed_claims: The actual real map is injective throughout every finite p>1 source space. The local-homeomorphism result then makes it an open embedding.
row.qualification: The constructed original package has no supplied global-injectivity premise.

row.requirement: The Hilbert base case and the cited external construction.
reviewed_claims: The Hilbert map is internally proved globally bijective: the action-mass identity bounds sources, coefficient compactness and actual action continuity prove properness, and the trace identity gives a singleton zero fiber.
A closed local homeomorphism with a singleton fiber over the connected target is bijective. Its inverse agrees locally with the analytic inverses.
This proves the mathematical Hilbert base case used by the section. Equality with the exact construction in the cited 2014 edition of [23], Theorem 19.3, remains unverified.
row.qualification: Partial denotes the retained external-edition comparison only. The internal Hilbert inverse is a proved theorem, not an assumption.

row.requirement: Local inverse branches and Hilbert collision reduction.
reviewed_claims: Two distinct preimages of a common output give local inverse branches. One sufficiently large finite truncation of that output lies in both inverse neighborhoods and has distinct preimages in independently prescribed source neighborhoods.

Finite output support means finitely many open spectral gaps. The finite-gap Sobolev bootstrap supplies coefficient-preserving Hilbert realizations, and exponent compatibility gives an actual Hilbert collision. Below two direct inclusion suffices.
row.qualification: This supplies the regularity step behind restricting inverse branches to Hilbert space. Openness of their intersections alone is not used as a proof of Hilbert preimages.

row.requirement: Proposition 17.3: surjectivity for 1<p<=2.
reviewed_claims: Every real target in exponent 1<p<=2 has a preimage under the actual source map. The full original package combines this with injectivity and analytic local inverses.
row.qualification: The upper bound p<=2 is retained in surjectivity and the global inverse.

row.requirement: Hilbert preimage and stronger-exponent membership goal.
reviewed_claims: Include the p-target into Hilbert space and apply the internally constructed Hilbert inverse. The proof then recovers membership of this actual Hilbert preimage in the original p-space.
The coefficient-preserving inclusions and map compatibility identify the final p-output with the prescribed target.
row.qualification: The contradiction formulation (3.5) and the direct recovery of p-membership prove the same conclusion. The exact cited 2014 identification remains qualified in S17-007.

row.requirement: Origin inverse chart and the small target ball (3.6).
reviewed_claims: The actual real map sends zero to zero and has an open image containing zero. Hence an actual positive-radius target ball lies in its image.
The complex local inverse from Proposition 17.1 also supplies the ambient chart around zero; restricting its target neighborhood permits any smaller ball, including the source notation B_(4 epsilon).
row.qualification: The surjectivity proof needs only the real small-ball consequence. Its radius is chosen from openness rather than fixed in advance.

row.requirement: Finite reduction strategy and source-space displacements.
reviewed_claims: Finite lists of actual Hilbert angle-flow moves are defined in their list order. Every admissible move stops strictly before its current collapse time.
The sum of the stronger-space displacements recovers both actual Fourier components of the total displacement in every finite exponent above one.
row.qualification: The initial Hilbert source need not itself belong to the stronger space. Membership is asserted for the displacement.

row.requirement: Original angle gradients, stronger-space Hamiltonian and (3.7).
reviewed_claims: The original theta sum has real analytic local representatives modulo pi on the selected open-gap domain, with its full branch-independent differential.

At conjugate exponents p<=2<=q, bounded recovery of the q-cotangent gives an exponent-p Hamiltonian vector analytic in the Hilbert source. Its Hilbert inclusion equals the actual theta Hamiltonian, even for independently constructed normalized families.
The lifted curve solves the original Hamiltonian equation (3.7). Only the selected gap must be open.
row.qualification: Angle values retain their period ambiguity; the vector field uses the well-defined differential. The selected open-gap condition replaces the inconsistent D_k/Z_k notation at real sources.

row.requirement: Actual finite reductions with the selected index m_n.
reviewed_claims: Finite selected actions can be made smaller than any prescribed positive index-dependent bounds by actual admissible flows. The finite-set induction skips already small actions and preserves all earlier bounds.
This includes the positive geometric thresholds used in the source. The selected gap and vector-field labels are m_n throughout the recursive construction.
row.qualification: The occurrences of Z_n and Y_n in the selected m_n step are corrected to Z_(m_n) and Y_(m_n). No new refutation is added.

row.requirement: Selected action decreases while other actions are preserved.
reviewed_claims: Along the original theta flow, I_j(t)=I_j(0)-t when j is the selected index and I_j(t)=I_j(0) otherwise. The formula holds for all times up to collapse, including negative times.
Consequently each later distinct selected move preserves the bounds already achieved. The finite induction proves all prescribed inequalities simultaneously.
row.qualification: The exact action law supplies the integrated content of the canonical commutator used here. The source time derivative has the negative unit sign.

row.requirement: Untouched enumeration tail with the correct m_k index.
reviewed_claims: Every unselected rectangular coordinate is preserved through the entire finite list. Therefore its original indexed action is preserved as well.
In the enumerated tail the retained equality is I_(m_k)(phi_n)=I_(m_k)(phi_0).
row.qualification: The printed right-hand index k is corrected to m_k. The finite-set formulation keeps the exact outside set.

row.requirement: Corrected coordinate-power sum constant and action budget.
reviewed_claims: For 1<p<=2 the correct pointwise bound is |x|^p+|y|^p <= 2*((x^2+y^2)/2)^(p/2). It follows from concavity of the p/2 power.

Both the coordinate-power sum and action-power sum are proved summable. The original spectral actions then satisfy the literal infinite summed bound with factor two, retaining both coordinate powers inside each summand.
row.qualification: The factor two is used directly. The literal summed power is distinguished from the maximum product norm used by the target interfaces. No new optimality or failure witness is proved.

row.requirement: Summable action tails and the 2N+1 enumeration cutoff.
reviewed_claims: Actual p-coordinates give summable original action powers. The one-based ordering 0,-1,1,-2,2,... is a proved bijection after shifting its natural-number index.
Its first 2N+1 positions cover exactly the modes with absolute index at most N. The remaining enumeration sum equals the absolute-mode tail with |m|>N.
row.qualification: The absolute cutoff N is paired with 2N+1 enumeration positions. The actual surjectivity proof instead uses a chosen finite set and its exact complement, so both descriptions retain the same tail scope.

row.requirement: Small target estimate and identification of the reduced source (3.8).
reviewed_claims: With factor two and an action-power budget below 2 epsilon^p, the coordinate-power sum is below 4 epsilon^p and hence below (4 epsilon)^p for p>=1. An existing general public example proves this positive arithmetic bound.
The actual finite-action criterion gives a small p-target from small selected actions and unchanged outside coordinates, even when the candidate initially lives only in Hilbert space.
An original p-preimage exists in the small image ball. Hilbert injectivity identifies it with the reduced Hilbert source, giving (3.8).
row.qualification: The corrected constant and matching cutoff preserve the original small-target argument. The implementation uses an arbitrary image-ball radius rather than depending on a norm equality for a product space.

row.requirement: Finite displacement recovers original p-membership.
reviewed_claims: An admissible finite reduction preserves membership in every exponent p<=2: the reduced source is the original source plus a source-p displacement.
Subtracting that displacement from the identified p-preimage recovers the original Hilbert preimage in p, finishing surjectivity.
row.qualification: Both coefficient components and their real-type relation are retained; mere coordinatewise regularity is not substituted for source-space membership.

row.requirement: Attribution of the flow method to reference [36].
reviewed_claims: The source attributes the method of the following flow lemma to reference [36], Lemma 1. The mathematical flow statement is proved internally in the next groups.
row.qualification: This records the attribution in the dissertation; it does not independently compare the external paper or certify the historical attribution.

row.requirement: Lemma 17.4: unique C1 flow and displacement in every finite exponent.
reviewed_claims: For every real Hilbert source with the selected gap open, the original theta Hamiltonian has a C1 solution on the complete interval (-infinity,I_k(phi_0)).
Uniqueness holds against every ambient complex-source solution with the same initial value and actual derivative equation. The selected action tends to zero at the right endpoint.
The displacement has a continuous real-type realization in every finite exponent r>1, with equality of every actual Fourier coefficient.
row.qualification: Only the selected gap is assumed open. No C1 extension through the collapse endpoint is asserted.

row.requirement: Hilbert canonical map and the original angle differential.
reviewed_claims: The Hilbert map is globally bi-real-analytic and has the actual canonical rectangular brackets. Positive-root action-angle formulas identify the original theta with the polar angle modulo its period.
On the selected open gap its full differential is (-y dx+x dy)/(2I). The identity remains valid when the map and auxiliary angle family were independently constructed.
row.qualification: The polar angle statement uses the original cosine/sine phase and local differential, not a globally single-valued analytic principal argument.

row.requirement: Equation (3.9) with inward signs in both components.
reviewed_claims: The actual Jacobian sends the original theta Hamiltonian to the radial field with both components negative: -x_k/(x_k^2+y_k^2) and -y_k/(x_k^2+y_k^2). Every other coordinate has zero velocity.
The coordinate radial curve scales the selected pair by sqrt(1-t/I_k(phi_0)), and its derivative is this field at the current point.
row.qualification: The positive printed x sign in (3.9) is replaced directly by the inward negative sign. Existing historical witnesses are preserved without new ones.

row.requirement: Full pre-collapse time interval, uniqueness and selected-action limit.
reviewed_claims: The positive selected action makes the radial scale smooth for every t<I_k(phi_0), including all negative times. The global analytic inverse lifts it to the actual source curve.
The vector field is C1 near every point of the reference curve. Local Lipschitz uniqueness propagates across the connected open time interval, and the exact selected-action law gives the zero limit.
row.qualification: The explicit curve also has a continuous source-norm collapse limit, but the differentiable ODE statement remains on the open interval.

row.requirement: Bochner integration in the stronger space gives continuous displacement.
reviewed_claims: For an exponent below two, the actual theta velocity has a continuous stronger-space realization and an actual Bochner integral on every segment from zero to t. Applying Hilbert inclusion commutes with that integral and recovers the source displacement.

Above two, continuous Hilbert inclusion supplies the displacement directly. In both cases both actual Fourier components agree, and the resulting displacement is continuous in the claimed stronger or weaker source norm.
row.qualification: The integral proof does not infer stronger-norm convergence from Hilbert convergence alone. The additional angle families are constructed internally and identified by exponent compatibility.

row.requirement: Original periodic isospectral sets and action tori.
reviewed_claims: The source isospectral set uses the actual periodic spectrum and algebraic multiplicities. The target torus fixes the quadratic radius at every signed index to the original spectral action.
The action-radius identity identifies the preimage of that torus with the original source action level set.
row.qualification: The action level set and the spectral isospectral set are distinct definitions; their equality below two is a proved later conclusion.

row.requirement: Compactness of the target torus for every finite exponent.
reviewed_claims: Every action torus is closed. If nonempty, any one element supplies a single lp majorant for all coordinate magnitudes of every other element.
Uniform majorant tails and closedness give compactness in the full target norm at every finite exponent. Empty tori and infinitely many nonzero actions are included.
row.qualification: Finite exponent is required. Coordinatewise compactness alone is not used to claim norm compactness.

row.requirement: Lemma 17.5: equality and compactness below two, inclusion above two.
reviewed_claims: For 1<p<=2 the actual isospectral image is the entire prescribed action torus and the source isospectral set is compact in its original norm.
For every finite p>1, hence also p>2, the isospectral image is contained in the torus.
row.qualification: Neither complete torus images nor source isospectral compactness above exponent two are asserted.

row.requirement: Equal periodic spectral data give equal discriminants and actions.
reviewed_claims: Equality of the actual periodic spectrum with multiplicities is equivalent to equality of the normalized discriminant. Equal endpoints also identify the canonically signed square root.
A common smaller action contour gives equality of each original indexed action, including collapsed gaps and the finite central block. This proves the all-exponent torus inclusion.
row.qualification: The normalization and spectral multiplicities are retained; equality of unlabelled zero sets alone is not substituted.

row.requirement: Hilbert action rotations and transfer of torus equality below two.
reviewed_claims: In Hilbert space the inverse map lifts every finite coordinate action rotation. Its actual source velocity is the action Hamiltonian, whose discriminant derivative is zero; every such source curve is isospectral.

Finite rotations can match any finite block of an equal-action target, and those replacements converge in the full norm. Continuity of the inverse and closedness of the actual isospectral set yield the converse inclusion.
Action and discriminant compatibility transfer this equality to p<=2. The global inverse maps the compact action torus to the compact source action level set, and the spectral set is closed.
row.qualification: This establishes the mathematical converse internally; the exact external [23] edition comparison remains the qualification in S17-007.

units.assessment_convention: Current ordered ledger; all historical supporting records retained.

row.requirement: Hamiltonian integral and complex NLS system (4.1).
reviewed_claims: The period-one H1 energy equals the literal integral of the kinetic and quartic terms. On smooth periodic complex pairs, its two directional derivatives are integration against the actual variational gradients.
The cross-component Hamiltonian field is (-i times the second gradient, +i times the first gradient), giving the matrix convention in (4.1).
row.qualification: The integral energy is defined on H1; pointwise Hamiltonian PDE identities use smooth periodic fields. No pointwise derivative is asserted for arbitrary L2 data.

row.requirement: Real-type scalar dNLS equation (4.2).
reviewed_claims: The Hamiltonian field preserves the conjugate-pair real form. Multiplication of its first component by i gives -u_xx + 2|u|^2 u.
row.qualification: The subsequent rough solutions use the explicit smooth-approximation definition, rather than imposing a classical PDE on distributions.

row.requirement: Sobolev canonical analytic Birkhoff diffeomorphism and weighted actions.
reviewed_claims: The actual weighted Birkhoff map has a global real analytic inverse at every nonnegative real Sobolev order in the range 1<p<=2, hence at p=2 and every printed integer order.

Canonical brackets retain the physical factor -i and the rectangular sign convention. Weighted spectral actions are summable at every positive integer Sobolev order; the Hilbert case supplies summable actions at order zero.
row.qualification: The mathematics is proved internally. Identification with the exact cited 2014 construction [23] remains qualified as in S17-007; inspecting the earlier 2013 manuscript does not close that external comparison.

row.requirement: Full Hamiltonian analyticity, action dependence and Taylor expansion.
reviewed_claims: The physical energy is analytic on the full complex H1 pair space and is recovered by the same action-only Hamiltonian on every real H1 source.
In the standard weighted ell^(2,1) action norm, H equals the weighted linear sum plus 2(sum I)^2 minus sum I_n^2, with one uniform cubic remainder bound near zero.
row.qualification: The bound includes complex infinite-support inputs in one ball. The attribution to [51] is historical; this comparison checks the internal expansion, not that external proof.

row.requirement: Full Hamiltonian origin derivatives with the mass correction.
reviewed_claims: At zero the full energy frequency is (2 pi n)^2. Restoring the mass term gives the full Hessian 4-2 delta_nm.
The Hessian -2 delta_nm belongs to H*, whose gradient is the renormalized nonlinear frequency.
row.qualification: Use the positive corrected derivative formula directly. Historical refutation proofs are unchanged and no new one is added.

row.requirement: Frequency Taylor expansion (4.3).
reviewed_claims: Literal coordinate derivatives of the full Hamiltonian equal dispersion + 4 sum I - 2 I_n + R_n.
A single Hilbert remainder sequence satisfies ||R||<=C||I||^2 in the standard weighted action norm, with radius and constant chosen before the action and spectral index.
row.qualification: This is the uniform sequence form of (4.3), retaining the corrected full-Hessian mass term.

row.requirement: Rectangular Birkhoff equations and rotation signs.
reviewed_claims: Every global ordinary solution in the original approximation class has rectangular coordinates satisfying xdot_n=-omega_n y_n and ydot_n=omega_n x_n.
These frequencies remain constant along that same solution.
row.qualification: The source overview is in the Hilbert/Sobolev range, contained in the proved 1<p<=2 range. The physical Hamiltonian time orientation is used.

row.requirement: Renormalized nonlinear frequency normalization.
reviewed_claims: The full action derivative restores exactly 4 times total action and the free dispersion to the same retained frequency F.
On actual real finite-gap potentials, the original action map recovers the independently constructed physical frequency with those terms subtracted.
row.qualification: The finite-gap physical normalization and the action-space derivative identity have their separate stated domains.

row.requirement: Hamiltonian H* including the weighted linear subtraction.
reviewed_claims: H* equals physical H minus 2 mass squared minus the literal absolutely convergent weighted action series on every real H1 source.
On the common connected action domain, the retained original frequency is exactly the gradient of this same H*.
row.qualification: Both subtractions are retained. H-2mass^2 alone is the renormalized PDE Hamiltonian Hr.

row.requirement: Renormalized frequency expansion at zero.
reviewed_claims: The same frequency vanishes at zero, has derivative -2Id, and has a quadratic remainder in the full action norm.
row.qualification: For every finite p>2 the action exponent is p/2; the neighborhood and bound are uniform over all coordinates.

row.requirement: Original action-image domain and analytic neighborhood.
reviewed_claims: The action domain is open and connected, contains all original real-source actions and the entire nonnegative summable cone, and is an actual action image.
More precisely U is the image of an open source neighborhood Y containing the real locus with Y contained in the original complex domain V.
row.qualification: The justified image statement uses a restricted source neighborhood. It does not identify U with the image of the entire previously chosen V. The stronger target realizations below imply the prior weaker weighted-frequency regularity.

row.requirement: Theorem 18.1: one frequency, all target exponents and mixed remainder.
reviewed_claims: One original Hilbert frequency has real and complex analytic realizations into every ell^r target with r>1, including infinity, on the same action domain.

For each finite p>2 an original family gives one analytic F on ell^(p/2) extending those nonnegative summable-action values. Its correction F+2I has one locally uniform ell^(p/3)+ell^(1+) decomposition chosen before all projection exponents.
row.qualification: The literal p/3 component is retained when it is below one. Infinity is a frequency target, not an extension to all bounded action inputs. The domain has the restriction stated in S18-011.

row.requirement: Motivation for applications to perturbations.
reviewed_claims: The passage motivates perturbative applications of the following frequency inverse results.
row.qualification: Possible applications are not a separate mathematical theorem or a proved perturbation result.

row.requirement: Corollary 18.2(i): local analytic inverse at zero.
reviewed_claims: The same frequency is a bijection between actual open neighborhoods of zero with an analytic inverse throughout its image. Its inverse derivative at zero is -1/2 Id.
row.qualification: The source neighborhood lies in the original action domain; global injectivity of the frequency is not asserted.

row.requirement: Corollary 18.2(ii): compact derivative correction.
reviewed_claims: At every complex action in the same domain, dF+2Id is compact, by factoring the refined derivative through a stronger Banach sequence space and applying Pitt compactness.
row.qualification: A finite exponent strictly between one and p/2 and at least p/3 is selected; no Banach structure is imposed on ell^(p/3) below one.

row.requirement: Corollary 18.2(iii): Fredholm index zero.
reviewed_claims: Every derivative is Fredholm with equal finite kernel and cokernel dimensions, giving index zero.
row.qualification: This is a statement throughout the original connected action domain, for each finite p>2.

row.requirement: Corollary 18.2(iv): generic local analytic inverse.
reviewed_claims: There is one open subset dense in the original domain where every point has an analytic inverse branch between open sets, with the inverse derivative equal to the inverse Jacobian.
row.qualification: Analytic Fredholm density uses connectedness and invertibility at zero. Inverse neighborhoods may depend on the point.

row.requirement: Corrected H* definition and local concavity claim.
reviewed_claims: The H* preceding Theorem 18.3 includes the weighted linear action subtraction, as in the earlier displayed definition.
The same Hamiltonian has an analytic FL4 extension and strict concavity on one neighborhood of zero in the real Hilbert action space.
row.qualification: The conjecture attribution is historical. The internal theorem proves local concavity; it does not assert global concavity on the entire positive Hilbert cone.

row.requirement: Theorem 18.3(i): FL4 extension, sign and zero set.
reviewed_claims: The actual original H* is analytic on an open complex FL4 neighborhood containing the full real locus. On real sources it is real, nonpositive, and zero exactly at the zero source.
row.qualification: The constructor retains the same original family, action frequency and physical H1 identity.

row.requirement: Theorem 18.3(ii): action extension, sign and local Hessian bound.
reviewed_claims: One open connected Hilbert action domain carries the same analytic Hamiltonian, with nonpositive real values and zero only at zero on its nonnegative part.
The Hessian at zero is -2 times the bilinear Hilbert pairing. On one positive-radius ball it obeys Re d2H*(J,J)<=-||J||^2 for every real Hilbert direction.
row.qualification: The positive domain is relatively open and dense; it is not replaced by the whole nonnegative Hilbert cone. Closed-gap boundary points are included in the local strict Jensen conclusion.

row.requirement: Remark 18.4: no C1 extension above action exponent two.
reviewed_claims: The same H* has no continuous, hence no C1, extension near zero relative to the nonnegative ell^q cone for any q>2, including infinity.
The proof integrates the local Hessian bound and uses finite nonnegative blocks; the infinity endpoint follows by coefficient-preserving inclusion.
row.qualification: This proves the source nonextension assertion by a stronger continuity obstruction. It is not an additional refutation of a printed constant.

row.requirement: Global Sobolev solutions and analytic trajectory map (4.4).
reviewed_claims: Constructed ordinary and renormalized global solutions have real analytic trajectory maps in the uniform Sobolev norm on each compact time interval, for every real regularity s>=0.
At p=2 this gives the Sobolev assertion (4.4). Uniqueness holds in the stated original all-smooth-approximation class.
row.qualification: The attribution to [7] is historical and is not an external proof comparison. Analyticity is in the initial datum with values in the trajectory space; no analyticity in time or uniqueness among arbitrary distributional solutions is inferred.

row.requirement: Ordinary frequency obstruction and renormalized frequency.
reviewed_claims: The renormalized PDE frequency is the ordinary frequency minus four times the physical mass H1, equivalently dispersion plus omega*.
The announced ordinary-flow continuity obstruction is proved for the actual smooth solution map in S18-035.
row.qualification: Read the isolated S1 in this display as the mass H1, consistent with the preceding expansion and the following Hamiltonian. This is a notation correction; no new refutation is added.

row.requirement: Renormalized Hamiltonian and Wick-ordered PDE (4.5).
reviewed_claims: The literal renormalized energy is H-2H1^2. Both variational gradients include the factor four in the mass term.
Its real-type Hamiltonian field gives -v_xx+2|v|^2v-4(integral |v|^2)v, and the constructed smooth trajectories satisfy that actual Hamiltonian equation.
row.qualification: Hr retains dispersion; H* subtracts it. The classical differential equation and the rough approximation solution class are distinguished.

row.requirement: Conserved mass and corrected gauge conversion.
reviewed_claims: The positive gauge phase is exp(4 i mass t), where mass is the squared L2 norm. The inverse phase recovers the ordinary solution.
Physical mass conservation and the gauge identity hold for the actual full source flows in 1<p<=2, hence for the Sobolev solutions.
row.qualification: The factor four and the square are retained directly. Historical constant-datum witnesses are unchanged.

row.requirement: Analytic Sobolev trajectories and local higher-exponent extension.
reviewed_claims: Both Sobolev trajectory maps are analytic for every compact time interval. At higher finite source exponents the renormalized map has a local analytic extension at every datum.
row.qualification: The extension sentence is interpreted with the immediately following local definition and Theorem 18.5(ii). It does not supply a global map on all higher-exponent sources for every prescribed time horizon.

row.requirement: Original all-smooth-approximation solution definition.
reviewed_claims: A solution is continuous on its time domain, starts at the prescribed datum, and is the pointwise source-norm limit of the actual classical trajectories for every convergent sequence of smooth initial data.
The smooth classical trajectories are constructed and satisfy the renormalized PDE with their own initial mass.
row.qualification: The general domain formulation requires zero in the domain and includes the printed open intervals and compact intervals used for wellposedness. Convergence is quantified over all smooth approximations.

row.requirement: Uniqueness in the stated solution class.
reviewed_claims: Smooth density and uniqueness of limits imply that two solutions with the same initial datum agree on the intersection of their time domains.
row.qualification: Uniqueness is precisely in the original approximation solution class.

row.requirement: Definition of local analytic wellposedness.
reviewed_claims: Local analytic wellposedness supplies a single positive time and an open neighborhood for each datum, solutions for every datum in that neighborhood, and a real analytic map into continuous trajectories with the uniform norm.
row.qualification: The neighborhood and time are chosen before the neighboring datum, exactly as required by (a) and (b).

row.requirement: Definition of global analytic wellposedness.
reviewed_claims: Global analytic wellposedness on an open initial-data set supplies one trajectory for all real times for each datum, with analytic compact-time restriction maps for every positive horizon.
row.qualification: The underlying global trajectories are chosen before the time horizon, as required by (a prime) and (b prime).

row.requirement: Transition to Fourier Lebesgue applications.
reviewed_claims: The passage introduces the Fourier Lebesgue applications of the preceding frequency theorem.
row.qualification: This transition adds no mathematical hypothesis or separate result.

row.requirement: Theorem 18.5(i): global wellposedness for 1<p<=2.
reviewed_claims: Renormalized NLS is globally real analytically wellposed on the whole source space for every finite 1<p<=2, in the original solution sense.
row.qualification: The spectral families and smooth solution construction are internal to the theorem; they are not additional premises.

row.requirement: Theorem 18.5(ii): local wellposedness for 2<p<infinity.
reviewed_claims: For every finite p>2, renormalized NLS is locally real analytically wellposed at every source, with analytic dependence in the complete compact trajectory norm.
row.qualification: The general implementation also covers finite 1<p<=2; the printed higher-exponent range is included.

row.requirement: Theorem 18.5(iii): small-data global wellposedness above two.
reviewed_claims: For every finite p>2 there is an open neighborhood of zero containing a positive source-norm ball where renormalized NLS is globally real analytically wellposed.
row.qualification: The neighborhood is constructed from the invariant coordinate-image region, and the same trajectories exist for all real times.

row.requirement: Theorem 18.5(iv): ordinary solution-map nonextension.
reviewed_claims: At every FLp source outside L2 with finite p>2, no map agreeing with all actual smooth ordinary solutions can be continuous into compact-time FLq trajectories.
The original package covers finite q>=p; the retained-family theorem includes infinity and even every q>=1.
row.qualification: The input exponent remains finite. Agreement is with constructed physical classical solutions, not arbitrary coordinate rotations.

row.requirement: Historical related wellposedness and weak-continuity results.
reviewed_claims: The passage surveys historical weak discontinuity, renormalized weak continuity, nonuniform continuity and real-line mapping results attributed to other authors.
row.qualification: These cited external results are recorded as historical context, not claimed as formalized or independently checked by this ordered review. The survey continues on page 87.

row.requirement: Historical announcements, open question and probabilistic results.
reviewed_claims: The continuation records an announcement, real-line weak-solution bounds, a then-open torus question and probabilistic wellposedness results.
row.qualification: Open status and literature priority are reported only as statements in the 2016 dissertation, not as current research status. No independent external-source comparison is claimed.

row.requirement: Historical Fourier Lebesgue existence and uniqueness classes.
reviewed_claims: The passage compares earlier Fourier Lebesgue constructions, continuity, solution methods and their distinct uniqueness classes.
row.qualification: These are historical attributions. The internal uniqueness theorem below uses the dissertation approximation class and does not subsume every external solution notion.

row.requirement: Contributions: analyticity, small global solutions and original-class uniqueness.
reviewed_claims: The implemented conclusions supply analytic initial-data dependence, small-data global solutions and uniqueness in the original all-smooth-approximation class.
The phase characterization uses the actual original coordinates; the ordinary solution map fails continuity at every higher-exponent source outside L2.
row.qualification: The sentence about one continuous solution is read in the solution sense defined on page 86 and characterized in Remark 22.3. It is not a claim of uniqueness among arbitrary distributional solutions; novelty is contextual.

row.requirement: Canonical differential product (4.6).
reviewed_claims: The full product uses the critical points lambda_m^bullet, with leading factor -i. It converges unconditionally, and symmetric cutoff products have the same limit.
row.qualification: Restore the missing critical-point bullet in (4.6). The existing positive product theorem supplies the correction directly.

row.requirement: Primitive and finite-gap Laurent overview.
reviewed_claims: The primitive is single valued and analytic on the complement of noncollapsed gaps. At every real finite-gap source it has a convergent physical Hamiltonian Laurent expansion in an exterior region.
row.qualification: The informal meromorphic statement is read at infinity. No global meromorphic continuation through open cuts is claimed.

row.requirement: Joint and filled spectral analyticity of the differential.
reviewed_claims: One open moving-cut joint domain supports the actual quotient and primitive differential; spectral slices fill collapsed gaps.
row.qualification: Read the indexed union in the printed fixed-exterior domain as the union of U_m. The implementation proves joint analyticity on the larger moving-cut domain of a common restricted source neighborhood containing the full real locus.

row.requirement: Definition by the average of endpoint integrals.
reviewed_claims: The original definition is the half-average of the two actual improper endpoint integrals, and equals the same normalized primitive.
row.qualification: The factor one half is literal; no integral value is supplied as an assumption.

row.requirement: Improper convergence and admissible path independence.
reviewed_claims: Every admissible interior C1 path and finite piecewise interior C1 path from either endpoint has the same improper integral. The two truncation parameters tend independently to their endpoints.
row.qualification: Convergence follows from the actual primitive derivative and endpoint limits. This replaces the informal singularity argument and needs no separate absolute-integrability premise for the improper limit; interiors and intermediate corners avoid the cuts.

row.requirement: Equality of the two endpoint integrals.
reviewed_claims: Each selected endpoint integral equals F_n, including when the gap collapses.
row.qualification: The root-complement filter is proved nontrivial at the endpoint, so equality does not come from a vacuous limit.

row.requirement: Analytic primitive despite lexicographic endpoint labels.
reviewed_claims: The endpoint-label discussion motivates constructing the analytic primitive without differentiating individual lexicographically chosen endpoints.
row.qualification: Joint analyticity is proved. This review does not add or claim a standalone theorem that the lexicographic endpoint maps fail continuity.

row.requirement: Lemma 19.1(i): joint analyticity and source gradient.
reviewed_claims: The same primitive is jointly analytic off the moving cuts, and its source Frechet derivative is the actual discriminant cotangent divided by the canonical root.
row.qualification: The source domain may be restricted inside the original Birkhoff domain; every real source remains. Spectral analyticity includes filled collapsed gaps.

row.requirement: Lemma 19.1(ii): index shift and endpoint values.
reviewed_claims: F_n=F_0+i*pi*n, and one relative endpoint extension has value i*pi*(n-j) at either endpoint of gap j.
row.qualification: Continuity is relative to the filled spectral domain with the selected endpoint adjoined, rather than continuation through the interior of an open cut.

row.requirement: Lemma 19.1(iii): locally uniform gap bound.
reviewed_claims: A single local source neighborhood and positive constant bound both boundary values by B*norm(gamma_n), for every signed index. The literal supremum range is bounded.
row.qualification: The quantifiers precede the index and side; there is no tail-only restriction.

row.requirement: Lemma 19.1(iv): analyticity of the square.
reviewed_claims: F_n squared is analytic off the noncollapsed cuts, and also has an agreeing analytic continuation across its own selected gap.
row.qualification: The selected-gap filling is stronger than the printed assertion, while other open gaps remain excluded.

row.requirement: Lemma 19.1(v): real arcosh boundary profiles.
reviewed_claims: For real sources the upper and lower boundary limits are respectively plus and minus arcosh of the signed half-discriminant on the entire closed gap.
row.qualification: The limits allow arbitrary approach from the corresponding open half-plane, including approach to endpoints.

row.requirement: Lemma 19.1(vi): exact free primitive.
reviewed_claims: At zero, F_n(z)=-i*z+i*pi*n=i*w_n(z).
row.qualification: This is an exact identity, including the filled zero gap.

row.requirement: Proof of joint and spectral analyticity.
reviewed_claims: Local joint charts agree with the actual global primitive, so its full moving-cut joint differential and filled spectral slices are proved.
row.qualification: This supplies the analytic continuation argument internally; the reference to Appendix F is navigational.

row.requirement: Positive real-gap companion expression.
reviewed_claims: The normalized primitive has exact exponential and companion-multiplier identities, and the real arcosh profile is continuous with zero endpoints and positive interior.
row.qualification: These results support the local logarithm construction, but this review has not identified a direct Lean statement for the printed strictly positive minimum of the real companion expression over the whole closed gap. That auxiliary assertion remains to be reconciled; the gradient theorem is already proved.

row.requirement: Positive real-gap companion expression.
reviewed_claims: The literal signed discriminant minus sqrt(Delta squared minus four) is strictly positive at every point of the closed real gap.
This continuous expression attains its minimum on the closed gap, and that minimum is strictly positive, including when the gap is collapsed.
row.qualification: The theorem uses the actual canonical discriminant for every real source at finite p>1 and every signed index. The exact minimum is supplied, with no open-gap, differentiability-of-endpoint-labels or separately assumed positivity premise.

row.requirement: Local contour and logarithm neighborhood.
reviewed_claims: An open neighborhood of each off-cut spectral/source point supports a normalized Floquet logarithm with the exact joint differential.
row.qualification: Use the selected index n consistently in U_n prime contained in U_n minus G_n. The signed multiplier is (-1)^n*(Delta+R)/2, with R the canonical root. The implementation uses local normalized logarithms and gluing, rather than requiring the printed single principal-log annulus.

row.requirement: Logarithmic primitive and gradient formula.
reviewed_claims: The exponential normalization is exact, and restricting the joint logarithm differential gives partial Delta divided by R.
row.qualification: Principal logarithms are used only where their branch is justified. No arbitrary additive period remains.

row.requirement: Analytic continuation of the source derivative.
reviewed_claims: The exact Floquet exponential identity propagates across the whole connected complex cut complement. Local normalized germs yield the full derivative at all off-cut points.
row.qualification: The argument uses proved agreement of germs and spectral uniqueness, not merely equality of squares.

row.requirement: Endpoint normalization and primitive shift.
reviewed_claims: The normalization shift and all endpoint constants are exact for every signed normalization and endpoint index.
row.qualification: The real normalization is continued to complex sources on the common domain.

row.requirement: Signed finite telescoping across bands.
reviewed_claims: The adjacent-band increment is -i*pi. Successor and predecessor induction give the complete signed-index shift.
row.qualification: Integer induction replaces the two displayed finite telescoping sums and includes negative indices.

row.requirement: Real-band canonical root and integral -i pi.
reviewed_claims: On the band after gap n, R=-i*(-1)^n*sqrt(4-Delta^2). Independent endpoint limits of the actual quotient integral give -i*pi.
row.qualification: The square root here is the nonnegative real root, multiplied by the displayed canonical phase. Collapsed adjacent gaps are allowed.

row.requirement: Canonical denominator in the continued shift formula.
reviewed_claims: The normalization integral and its source continuation use Delta prime divided by the canonical root R. They give F_0-F_n=-i*pi*n.
row.qualification: Keep R in the p.89 normalization paragraph. The printed positive root sqrt(4-Delta^2) omits the canonical phase; the earlier real-band calculation retains that phase explicitly.

row.requirement: Selected-gap differential factorization (4.7).
reviewed_claims: Separating the selected critical factor gives Delta prime/R=((lambda_n^bullet-z)/w_n)*(-i*chi_n), with chi_n analytic through the selected gap.
row.qualification: The deleted product is the actual spectral product and is analytic on the domain excluding only the other cuts.

row.requirement: Opposite boundary values and analytic square filling.
reviewed_claims: The opposite sides give opposite normalized primitive profiles. Their squares agree with an analytic continuation through the selected closed gap.
row.qualification: The analytic square extension includes both endpoints and collapsed gaps; continuity alone is not assumed to imply holomorphy without the implemented extension argument.

row.requirement: Collapsed-gap clause and all-index gap bound.
reviewed_claims: The collapsed selected gap has F_n=0; the same local all-index bound holds for every noncollapsed gap.
row.qualification: In the collapsed-gap sentence, replace F by F_n. The zero-index F at gap n has value -i*pi*n. The bound uses magnitudes for complex gaps.

row.requirement: Real-gap integral and arcosh value.
reviewed_claims: The real upper-side partial quotient integral equals the positive arcosh profile; the lower-side integral is its negative. Endpoint integrability is proved.
row.qualification: The canonical sheet orientation fixes the sign; the result holds across the whole closed real gap.

row.requirement: Free differential and free primitive.
reviewed_claims: The exact free primitive is -i*z+i*pi*n, with spectral derivative -i away from the cuts.
row.qualification: The free identity fixes both the derivative sign and the additive normalization.

row.requirement: Notation F=F0.
reviewed_claims: F denotes F_0; the relationship F=F_n-i*pi*n is already proved.
row.qualification: This is a notation declaration.

row.requirement: Figure 4.1 boundary sign picture.
reviewed_claims: Figure 4.1 illustrates boundary directions and signs, with zero endpoint values. Exact real-gap arcosh and real-band arcsine formulas provide the corresponding mathematical values.
row.qualification: The labels +1, -1, +i and -i indicate directions/signs, not constant magnitudes. The diagram is not an additional numerical-value theorem.

row.requirement: Lemma 19.2: convergent physical Hamiltonian Laurent series.
reviewed_claims: Every real finite-gap source at finite p>1 has a convergent exterior Laurent series whose coefficients are the physical NLS Hamiltonians. One radius works for all normalization indices.
row.qualification: The smooth periodic representative and its discriminant equality are constructed, not supplied as hypotheses.

row.requirement: Finite product, exterior growth and coefficient determination.
reviewed_claims: The finitely many noncollapsed cuts have compact union. The actual quotient is bounded in an exterior region, has a normalized analytic inversion germ, and the primitive has a convergent Laurent expansion with leading term -i*z and zero additional constant.
row.qualification: Exterior circle bounds, maximum modulus and the zero outer period replace the printed finite-product growth shortcut. The proof does not require a global meromorphic continuation across open cuts.

row.requirement: Real-band monotonicity and root sign.
reviewed_claims: The canonical root has the exact signed imaginary square-root expression, and the discriminant lies strictly between -2 and 2 in each open real band.
row.qualification: The printed strict monotonicity of (-1)^(n+1)*Delta on the whole closed band is not established by the two cited statements alone. A direct monotonicity theorem remains to be reconciled; the following arcsine derivative and band-value conclusions are independently proved.

row.requirement: Real-band monotonicity and root sign.
reviewed_claims: The signed discriminant (-1)^(n+1)*Delta is strictly increasing on the complete closed band from lambda_n^plus to lambda_(n+1)^minus, with exact endpoint values -2 and 2.
Every interior band point avoids all actual critical points, and the canonical root has the previously proved signed imaginary square-root expression.
row.qualification: Complete critical-point localization excludes derivative zeros in the open band. Rolle gives injectivity, and continuity plus the exact endpoint levels gives strict increase on the closed band. All signed indices and collapsed adjacent gaps are included.

row.requirement: Derivative of the real-band arcsine branch.
reviewed_claims: The real-band arcsine expression differentiates to the actual oriented canonical quotient.
row.qualification: The implementation writes the equivalent i*(-1)^n*arcsin(Delta/2) expression and proves the discriminant is in the open arcsine interval.

row.requirement: Exact primitive on a real spectral band.
reviewed_claims: On each real open band, F equals the arcsine primitive minus i*pi/2-i*pi*n. The band primitive is continuous and its endpoint values are plus and minus i*pi/2.
row.qualification: Endpoint values are read through the proved relative limits. The full primitive agrees with the real-source primitive used in this formula.

row.requirement: Half-integer discriminant asymptotics.
reviewed_claims: The actual smooth periodic discriminant differs from 2*cos(i*sigma_N) by at most C/(2*abs(r))^N for every real abs(r)>=1, hence also at both tails of the half-integer sample sequence.
row.qualification: This is an internal all-order WKB proof with physical Hamiltonians. It does not assert an independent comparison with the exact cited edition of [23].

row.requirement: Uniform arcsine error transfer.
reviewed_claims: At every real zero of cosine, one local inverse estimate controls small phase differences by the discriminant error, with a neighborhood independent of the sample index.
row.qualification: This is an alternative proof of the required error transfer using complex sinh near zero. The displayed principal-arcsine difference is not separately exported or claimed as a literal Lean theorem.

row.requirement: Primitive approximation along half-integer points.
reviewed_claims: The normalized analytic phase has an order-N error against the physical Hamiltonian correction on every escaping positive sequence of real cosine zeros.
row.qualification: The implemented sampled phase estimate supplies the needed approximation directly, without the intermediate principal-arcsine formula. Its discriminant identity is proved for the actual full primitive.

row.requirement: Hamiltonian convention relative to reference 23.
reviewed_claims: The footnote explains a convention change relative to reference [23]. The internal construction fixes the physical Hamiltonians through the differential recurrence.
row.qualification: No independent comparison of the external book conventions is claimed in this review.

row.requirement: Sine addition, branch selection and Laurent coefficients.
reviewed_claims: The half-integer sample error determines every Taylor coefficient of the normalized analytic inversion phase. These coefficients form a genuinely convergent physical Hamiltonian series.
row.qualification: The proof explicitly chooses pi*(j+1/2), proves cosine vanishes there, and applies analytic order uniqueness. The local sinh estimate replaces the printed sine-addition/principal-arcsine branch calculation.

row.requirement: Transition to the cubic expansion.
reviewed_claims: The sentence introduces the cubic expansion used later.
row.qualification: This is a transition, not a separate assertion.

row.requirement: Corollary 19.3: cubic Laurent part and remainder.
reviewed_claims: The cubic Laurent part is i*z^3-(3*i/2)*H1*z-(3*i/4)*H2-(3*i/8)*(H3-2*H1^2)/z. The error is bounded by K/norm(z)^2 in every exterior complex direction.
row.qualification: The shifted normalizations share one radius and one positive bound before the index is chosen.

row.requirement: Lemma 19.4: locally uniform mixed gap error.
reviewed_claims: The literal two-sided gap-error supremum equals gamma_n*(g_n+h_n), with fixed locally bounded g in ell^(p/2) and h in every finite ell^q, q>1.
row.qualification: The supremum range is bounded before sSup is used. The sequences are chosen before all auxiliary exponents, and the quasi-norm range p/2<1 is retained. No analyticity of the bounding sequences is claimed.

row.requirement: Exact zero-potential error clause.
reviewed_claims: At zero the gap error vanishes exactly.
row.qualification: This retains the precise free normalization, with no asymptotic remainder.

row.requirement: Endpoint integral with the selected-gap product.
reviewed_claims: The actual endpoint integral uses the selected critical factor and the deleted product chi_n.
row.qualification: The integral and factorization refer to the same canonical quotient and the same selected gap.

row.requirement: Critical displacement and refined product estimate.
reviewed_claims: The exact squared-gap critical offset and the refined deleted-factor estimates supply locally uniform ell^(p/2)+ell^(1+) gap-error majorants.
row.qualification: The proof retains the actual critical displacement and the factor pi; quasi-norm addition is used when p/2<1. Finite central gaps are included by the final mixed-data constructor.

row.requirement: Product-error supremum estimate.
reviewed_claims: If D bounds abs(lambda_n^bullet-z) and E bounds abs(chi_n(z)-1) over the closed gap, both boundary errors satisfy abs(F_n-i*w_n)<=pi*(D*E+abs(lambda_n^bullet-tau_n)).
row.qualification: Use norms and retain the factor pi in the p.91 estimate. The existing positive comparison theorem supplies a sufficient complete error bound directly; no optimality claim or new refutation is added.

row.requirement: Standard-root derivative and elementary primitive.
reviewed_claims: Subtracting i*w_k from the primitive gives a numerator defect equal to the deleted-factor error plus the critical-to-midpoint offset. Integrating this defect yields the complete positive error bound.
row.qualification: The exclusion in the printed derivative sentence must use G_k when differentiating w_k. The implementation uses the equivalent quadratic differential equation, avoiding a separate branch-dependent primitive formula.

row.requirement: Collapsed gaps and reciprocal-root integral bound.
reviewed_claims: Collapsed gaps have zero error. For noncollapsed gaps the standard-root side-integral estimate retains pi, and the critical offset is included in the complete comparison bound.
row.qualification: A constant numerator in the normalized side-integral bound gives the reciprocal-root estimate. The later sequence estimate absorbs the fixed factor pi into its locally uniform majorants.

reviewed_claims: Q.zeta_analytic proves regular negative product analytic on the omitted-gap domain. Q.auxiliary_analytic restricts that domain by excluding tau_n. On an isolating selected disk use k!=n. No new pole counterexample is needed.

reviewed_claims: Order zero is exactly 2*pi*Kronecker delta from normalized psi periods, without an extra imaginary unit.
