row.qualification: This retains the quantifier order and the strict positivity of the constant in (A.1).

row.requirement: Least distribution order
reviewed_claims: The order is the least natural number satisfying the finite-order estimate, including for the zero functional.
row.qualification: The chosen order is minimal, rather than an arbitrary available upper bound.

row.requirement: Unique continuous extension and complex measure representation (A.2)
reviewed_claims: Order zero is equivalent to a unique continuous extension to the physical continuous-function space.
Every such extension has a unique complex-measure representation with the exact factor 1/L.
row.qualification: The measure representation and continuous integral modules were read in full; the normalized action is retained.

row.requirement: Regular complex Borel measures and order-zero equivalence
reviewed_claims: Actual complex measures have finite variation and regular variation on the compact physical circle.
They correspond bijectively to original distributions of least order zero.
row.qualification: The Radon qualification uses the actual Borel measure and its variation, not a renamed bounded functional.

row.requirement: Original normalized L1 action
reviewed_claims: An interval-integrable function defines an order-zero original distribution with action (1/L) times the integral of the function times the test.
row.qualification: The pairing is complex bilinear and contains no implicit conjugation.

row.requirement: Fourier coefficients and uniqueness
reviewed_claims: The nth coefficient is evaluation on the negative physical mode exp(-i*2*pi*n*x/L).
All coefficients determine the original distribution uniquely and agree with normalized integrals on L1 data.
row.qualification: Positive periods and signed indices, including zero, are retained.

row.requirement: Theorem A.1(i), growth at the least order
reviewed_claims: A distribution with finite order N has cofinite two-sided Fourier growth O(|n|^N), with the same N.
row.qualification: The claim includes N=0 and applies in particular at the least order. The asymptotic does not restrict the zero Fourier coefficient.

row.requirement: Theorem A.1(ii), polynomial synthesis and uniqueness
reviewed_claims: Every polynomially growing complex sequence has exactly one realization on all original smooth periodic tests.
row.qualification: The coefficient at zero is arbitrary, and uniqueness is on the full original distribution space.

row.requirement: Distributional derivative and physical Fourier multiplier
reviewed_claims: The distributional derivative is minus the transpose of the physical test derivative.
Its nth coefficient is i*2*pi*n/L times the original coefficient.
row.qualification: The formula includes negative and zero frequencies and arbitrary positive periods.

row.requirement: Original Fourier-Lebesgue spaces, norms, completeness and reflexivity
reviewed_claims: The original Fourier-Lebesgue subtype has exactly the weighted coefficient norm.
It is complete for all Banach exponents and reflexive for 1<p<infinity.
row.qualification: The Sobolev weight is the Section 2 weight (1+|n|)^s. Its tempered inverse supplies the original distribution realization.

row.requirement: Fourier-series norm convergence and infinity endpoint
reviewed_claims: Finite Fourier polynomials converge in the original Fourier-Lebesgue norm for every finite Banach exponent.
At infinity, this norm convergence holds exactly when the weighted coefficients tend to zero.
For every exponent, the same truncations converge when evaluated against each original smooth test.
row.qualification: Retain the weighted-c0 condition at infinity. Testwise convergence is not asserted to be strong-dual convergence. No new refutation is needed.

row.requirement: Sobolev identification, physical L2 and Parseval
reviewed_claims: The p=2 Fourier-Lebesgue norm is the Fourier definition of the Sobolev norm.
At s=0 it is isometric to the actual physical L2 quotient under normalized Haar measure, with the exact 1/L interval Parseval factor.
row.qualification: The normalization is explicit. The later interval Sobolev equivalence is not claimed to be an isometry.

row.requirement: L1 Fourier bound and interpolation transition
reviewed_claims: Every physical L1 Fourier coefficient and the FL-infinity norm are bounded by the normalized L1 norm.
row.qualification: The interpolation transition is realized by the continuous maps in A.2; the introductory comparison of spaces is context.

row.requirement: Lemma A.2 conjugate exponent embedding
reviewed_claims: For 1<=p<=2 and conjugate q, the actual physical Lp quotient embeds continuously and injectively into original FLq, with norm at most one.
row.qualification: The rendered source uses L^(p-prime) to FLp for 2<=p<=infinity. This is the same assertion after renaming the conjugate exponents; the prime is not discarded.

row.requirement: Lemma A.3 one distribution in all FLp above two that is not a measure
reviewed_claims: One original distribution, chosen before all p>2, belongs to every such FLp including infinity and is not represented by any actual complex measure.
row.qualification: This is the source existential assertion A.3. Its witness is retained; it is not an added refutation of a printed formula.

row.requirement: Absolute Fourier synthesis and continuous representative
reviewed_claims: Original FL1 elements have absolute and uniform physical Fourier synthesis with sup norm bounded by the FL1 norm.
The resulting uniformly continuous function is the unique continuous representative of the entire distribution.
row.qualification: The convergence is in the actual continuous-function sup norm, at the original physical period.

row.requirement: Wiener algebra and pseudomeasure dual
reviewed_claims: Original FL1 is a complete commutative normed Wiener algebra with norm-one identity and an injective continuous representative algebra map.
FL-infinity is isometrically the continuous dual of FL1, with the bilinear pairing using opposite signed Fourier indices.
row.qualification: The source says this algebra fact is not subsequently used; it is nevertheless implemented on the original distribution carrier.

row.requirement: Lemma A.4 reverse conjugate exponent embedding
reviewed_claims: For 1<=p<=2, original FLp embeds continuously and injectively into the physical Lq quotient for the conjugate exponent, with norm at most one and a unique representing class.
row.qualification: The conjugate prime was checked on the rendered page. At p=1 the map agrees with continuous synthesis, and at p=2 with the established isometry.

row.requirement: Lemma A.5 one continuous function outside all FLp below two
reviewed_claims: For every positive period, one continuous function lies outside all original FLp with 1<=p<2.
row.qualification: The proved membership criterion is exactly p>=2, including infinity. The same witness is used for all excluded exponents.

row.requirement: Printed chirp and its physical period
reviewed_claims: The printed coefficients exp(i*n*log n)/(sqrt(n)*log(n)^2), n>=2, give uniform convergence of ordinary positive-index cutoffs on the entire real line.
The literal phase exp(i*n*pi*x) has period two. At period L use the explicitly proved rescaling x to 2*x/L, giving phase exp(i*2*pi*n*x/L).
row.qualification: The physical period is corrected directly. The public uniform-convergence interfaces were read; this review does not repeat every transitive oscillatory estimate.

row.requirement: Remark A.6 Riemann-Lebesgue decay
reviewed_claims: Fourier coefficients of every physical L1 function tend to zero along the cofinite filter on signed integer frequencies.
row.qualification: This gives the actual continuous L1-to-c0 Fourier map.

row.requirement: Remark A.6 nonsurjectivity and contextual characterization
reviewed_claims: The physical L1-to-c0 Fourier map is not surjective; its range is dense and nonclosed.
The proof uses open mapping and actual Rudin-Shapiro polynomials.
row.qualification: The source remark about a useful characterization remaining unknown is historical context, not a theorem that no characterization can exist. Nonsurjectivity itself is part of A.6.

row.requirement: Convolution criterion, growth and convergence conventions
reviewed_claims: An original distributional Fourier product exists uniquely exactly when the convolution genuinely converges at each frequency and the resulting coefficients have polynomial growth.
row.qualification: Unordered HasSum and symmetric integer cutoffs have separate explicit criteria. Do not replace convergence by a default-valued tsum or omit output growth. Historical examples are unchanged.

row.requirement: Lemma A.7 product and exact Young bound (A.3)
reviewed_claims: Every Banach Young triple, including infinity endpoints, gives absolutely convergent convolution coefficients and a unique original product.
The bilinear product has exact operator norm one and is independent of the representing exponents.
row.qualification: Agreement with pointwise multiplication is retained for continuous factors when one factor is Wiener. The constant in (A.3) remains one.

row.requirement: Lemma A.8 embedding and corrected product constant (A.4)
reviewed_claims: For each finite Banach p, the FL^(1,p)-to-FL1 inclusion is continuous, injective and preserves the original distribution.
The product estimate retains the inverse-weight Holder factor C_p, with C_p<=2*p.
row.qualification: Correct (A.4) directly to norm(u*v)<=C_p*norm(u)*norm(v). The theorem includes p=1 and adds no infinity endpoint or new refutation.

row.requirement: Inverse-weight Holder factor and physical weight convention
reviewed_claims: C_p is the conjugate-sequence norm of the reciprocal weight (1+|n|)^(-1).
That reciprocal sequence belongs to every conjugate exponent above one, including infinity, and the original norm convention stays fixed.
row.qualification: Use the exact Section 2 weight. The physical rescaling (1+|2*n/L|) in the printed proof is not silently substituted for it. The finite factor is retained in the corrected estimate.

row.requirement: Interval sources and periodic boundary mismatch
reviewed_claims: Arbitrary interval Sobolev data need not satisfy periodic endpoint matching; the following embeddings accept this general input.
row.qualification: Read this as motivation about general interval data, not as universal nonmembership in FL1 for every input. No new negative theorem is added.

row.requirement: Lemma A.9 exponent ranges, including half regularity
reviewed_claims: For 0<=s<1/2, original interval data embeds into FLq whenever q>1/(s+1/2).
At s=1/2 the result holds for every q>1. L2 supplies all q>=2, including infinity, and ordinary L2 handles s=0.
row.qualification: Positive regularity uses actual finite Slobodeckij interval energy. No endpoint matching is required, and zero regularity does not use the fractional graph norm at s=0.

row.requirement: Subcritical interval-periodic Sobolev identification
reviewed_claims: For 0<s<1/2, the genuine intrinsic interval Sobolev space is continuously linearly equivalent to original FL^(s,2).
Both directions preserve physical representatives and have explicit analysis and synthesis norm bounds.
row.qualification: The identification retains the exact Section 2 Fourier weight and physical dilation constants; it is not asserted isometric. The s=0 case is ordinary L2.

row.requirement: Holder proof, reciprocal exponent and endpoint handling
reviewed_claims: The subcritical Holder argument gives the stated finite exponent range with explicit physical bounds.
The L2 inclusion handles q>=2 and infinity; the separate half-regularity construction handles q>1.
row.qualification: The reciprocal-exponent formula is used in its finite Holder range. The remaining endpoints use the separate verified maps, preserving the original normalized interval action.

units.assessment_convention: Current ordered ledger; all historical supporting records retained.

row.requirement: Conjugate exponent convention
reviewed_claims: The source uses the usual reciprocal conjugate-exponent convention; B.1 uses finite conjugate exponents and B.2 admits infinity.
row.qualification: The introductory notation is interpreted separately at the stated ranges of each lemma; it does not define the zero powers in B.3.

row.requirement: Lemma B.1, both reciprocal-series bounds
reviewed_claims: For every nonnegative shift alpha and finite conjugate pair p,q>1, the actual series over m>=1 is summable.
Its sum is at most (q+alpha)/(q-1)/(1+alpha)^q, which is at most p/(1+alpha)^(q-1).
row.qualification: Both printed constants and the alpha=0 case are retained. The natural-index implementation uses m=n+1 exactly.

row.requirement: Integral comparison retaining the first summand
reviewed_claims: The decreasing reciprocal-power series is bounded by its first summand plus the exact improper integral.
row.qualification: The first summand is retained before the algebraic simplification; no larger unspecified constant is substituted.

row.requirement: Lemma B.2, full Young inequality
reviewed_claims: Every Banach Young triple, including every infinity endpoint, gives a unique target sequence with a genuine HasSum formula at each output frequency.
The convolution is absolutely convergent in each row and its target norm is at most the product of input norms, with exact bilinear operator norm one.
row.qualification: The proof applies to arbitrary sequence inputs without finite-support assumptions; finite cutoffs and the lp Fatou property construct the actual limit.

row.requirement: Transition to the nested three-sequence estimate
reviewed_claims: The next result is a nested three-sequence version of the preceding Young estimate.
row.qualification: The prose reference to the preceding inequality is contextual. The following statement is compared using its actual nested magnitude formula.

row.requirement: Lemma B.3, finite positive exponent formula
reviewed_claims: For finite alpha,beta>0, gamma>=p1>=beta and p2,p3>=alpha with the printed reciprocal identity, all three nested sum levels converge.
The exact displayed bound has constant one and retains the indices k-l,l-m,m and powers beta/alpha,gamma/beta,1/gamma. Input exponents below one are allowed.
row.qualification: The divisions require strictly positive auxiliary exponents. The source supplies no zero-exponent definition or separate infinity/supremum convention; the implemented statement is explicitly finite and positive. Historical diagnostics remain unchanged and no new refutation is added.

row.requirement: Inner sequence and corrected outer gamma power
reviewed_claims: The inner sequence d_l is the positive alpha-th root of the actual sum of |b(l-m)*c(m)|^alpha, with its proved target membership and norm bound.
The next displayed outer sum is bounded by norm(a)^gamma*norm(d)^gamma and ultimately by norm(a)^gamma*norm(b)^gamma*norm(c)^gamma. Its positive gamma-th root is the stated B.3 left side.
row.qualification: Correct the proof wording to the gamma-th power of the left side. Powered complex sequences mean powered magnitudes in the actual construction. The new outer-sum theorem retains summability and constant one; the positive theorem passed its full check and is committed and pushed.

row.requirement: First powered Young relation (B.2)
reviewed_claims: The first powered Young application uses the exact relation 1/beta+1/gamma=1/p1+1/q and exponents p1,q,gamma at least beta.
row.qualification: The powered exponents are Banach even when original exponents are below one. The intermediate q is a positive finite real number.

row.requirement: Intermediate exponent order equivalence
reviewed_claims: Under the exact first reciprocal identity and positive finite exponents, q>=beta is equivalent to gamma>=p1.
row.qualification: Both directions are proved by reciprocal order, not only the direction needed by the final inequality. The positive proof step passed its full check and is committed and pushed.

row.requirement: Second powered Young estimate and (B.3)
reviewed_claims: The second powered Young application uses 1/alpha+1/q=1/p2+1/p3, with p2,p3,q at least alpha.
It bounds the norm of d by the product of the b and c norms and preserves the exact power-norm identities.
row.qualification: All inner sums are proved convergent before the positive root and the second convolution are formed.

row.requirement: Intermediate exponent at least alpha
reviewed_claims: The second reciprocal identity and p2,p3>=alpha imply that the constructed intermediate exponent q is at least alpha.
row.qualification: The construction uses the positive reciprocal 1/beta+1/gamma-1/p1, proves its bound by 1/alpha, and then inverts it. Its positivity is explicit.

row.requirement: Equivalence of the combined and two intermediate relations
reviewed_claims: The single mixed exponent condition is equivalent to the existence of a q satisfying both powered Young relations.
Adding (B.2) and (B.3) and cancelling 1/q recovers the printed combined identity; the order equivalence recovers gamma>=p1.
row.qualification: The new theorem provides the reverse implication as well as the existing constructive direction. The positive proof step passed its full check and is committed and pushed.

units.assessment_convention: Current ordered ledger; all historical supporting records retained.

row.requirement: Context and classical discrete Hilbert transform
reviewed_claims: The appendix recalls the discrete Hilbert transform on complex sequence spaces and then treats two perturbed lattices.
row.qualification: The literature attribution is contextual; the public implementation supplies the actual operators and convergent series.

row.requirement: C.1 corrected bounded transform statement
reviewed_claims: For every finite 1<p<infinity, there is a unique bounded complex linear operator whose output is the genuinely convergent omitted-diagonal series sum x_m/(m-n).
The signed denominator, all infinite-support inputs and absolute convergence are retained.
row.qualification: Use the corrected boundedness statement. The existing review records the historical correction to the printed isomorphism assertion; that evidence is preserved unchanged. This comparison adds no refutation and does not repeat or extend the obstruction proof.

row.requirement: Unperturbed lattice normalization
reviewed_claims: The reference lattice is sigma0_n=pi*n; the modified transform includes the outer factor pi.
A common constant complex displacement in both lattices gives precisely the ordinary transform.
row.qualification: The common displacement cancels in every off-diagonal denominator. The omitted diagonal stays omitted even when the two displaced lattices differ there.

row.requirement: C.2 displacement and separation assumptions
reviewed_claims: Both displacement sequences may be arbitrary bounded complex sequences.
For c>0, the exact hypothesis is c^(-1)*norm(m-n)<=norm(rho_m-sigma_n) for every m!=n.
row.qualification: No smallness, reality, ordering or finite-support assumption is introduced. The separation is required only off the diagonal.

row.requirement: Actual modified transform and uniform bound
reviewed_claims: For each finite 1<p<infinity, the actual series pi*sum_{m!=n} x_m/(rho_m-sigma_n) defines a unique bounded complex linear operator.
One bound is chosen before the two lattices from p,c and displacement norm bounds S,R; it is C_p+c*(S+R)*norm(square kernel).
row.qualification: The quantifier order is uniform over every separated pair with these norm bounds. The full transform is asserted only for finite 1<p<infinity; the correction operators separately extend to both Banach endpoints.

row.requirement: Reciprocal kernel identity
reviewed_claims: Subtracting the ordinary kernel gives exactly (s_n-r_m)/((m-n)*(rho_m-sigma_n)).
The separate two-denominator kernel is bounded by c times the summable reciprocal-square kernel, and the joint correction bound uses c*(norm(s)+norm(r)).
row.qualification: The zero diagonal and signed difference are accounted for before forming the absolutely convergent row sums. The new separate-kernel bound passed its full check and is committed and pushed.

row.requirement: Separate F/G operators with corrected labels
reviewed_claims: F uses the output displacement s_n and G uses the input displacement r_m in the two exact source series.
The resulting bounded operators satisfy correction=F-G and A=H+F-G.
row.qualification: Correct the swapped labels in the displayed decomposition directly. Both operators depend on both lattices; the labels specify which displacement appears in the numerator. These positive theorems passed their full check and are committed and pushed.

row.requirement: Pointwise and powered norm estimates with explicit separation constant
reviewed_claims: The pointwise F bound is c*norm(s)*the positive square-kernel convolution of abs(x).
At every finite Banach exponent, the powered sum is bounded by c^p*norm(s)^p times the powered majorant sum.
The final F estimate retains c^p*norm(s)^p*norm(square kernel)^p*norm(x)^p explicitly.
row.qualification: The source already displays c^p in the first estimate. Keep it explicit in the final estimate as well instead of hiding its dependence in C_p. All powered sums converge; these positive theorems passed their full check and are committed and pushed.

row.requirement: Young convolution estimate and analogous G estimate
reviewed_claims: Young convolution with the summable reciprocal-square kernel bounds the majorant on every Banach coefficient space.
F and G individually have norm bounds c*norm(s or r)*norm(square kernel)*norm(x), including p=1 and infinity; the finite-p G power estimate is explicit.
row.qualification: The finite-p powered G sum uses the input displacement norm. Adding the ordinary transform gives the original finite 1<p<infinity C.2 scope. These positive theorems passed their full check and are committed and pushed.

units.assessment_convention: Current ordered ledger; all historical supporting records retained.

row.requirement: Absolute versus ordinary ordered products
reviewed_claims: Absolute convergence of the ordered source products is equivalent to summability of the perturbation norms.
Absolute convergence gives genuine complex product convergence, including products with zero factors.
row.qualification: The source uses cutoffs from 1 through N. The public theorems retain these literal cutoffs. Historical evidence separating ordinary and absolute convergence is preserved without adding or repeating a refutation.

row.requirement: D.1 signed sum and square sum estimate
reviewed_claims: The norm of the actual complex product minus one is at most A*exp(S)+B*exp(S+S^2), with A the norm of the signed complex sum, B the sum of squared norms and S the sum of norms.
Absolute summability and the half-unit bound are retained; the printed constants and powers are unchanged.
row.qualification: The result holds over any index type, hence in particular over the two-sided integer lattice. The proof controls the logarithmic remainder by B.

row.requirement: D.2 exponential bound
reviewed_claims: The product error is bounded by exp(S)-1, which is at most S*exp(S).
row.qualification: Absolute summability suffices; the weaker bound does not require the half-unit hypothesis.

row.requirement: D.3 signed linear subtraction
reviewed_claims: Subtract the signed complex sum in the linear term and retain its squared norm divided by two in the exponential bound.
row.qualification: The symbol A in the subtraction is the complex sum, while D.1 used its norm. This is the positive corrected statement. Historical source-notation evidence is unchanged; no new refutation is added.

row.requirement: Sine product normalization
reviewed_claims: The free sine function is the limit of the literal negative symmetric root products.
The zero-index normalization denominator is one; all nonzero denominators are pi*m.
row.qualification: The negative prefactor, two-sided symmetric cutoffs and zero-index convention are retained. The product is not replaced by an arbitrarily normalized entire function.

row.requirement: Finite exponent displaced roots and uniform simple-root separation
reviewed_claims: Every finite Banach displacement exponent, including p=1, has the prescribed perturbed lattice.
If its roots are pairwise distinct, one strictly positive constant separates every pair of distinct roots.
row.qualification: Uniform separation uses finite-exponent decay. For arbitrary bounded displacements only the individual-root isolation used later is asserted; a common global separation is not inferred from boundedness alone.

row.requirement: Adaptation from p=2
reviewed_claims: The source says its presentation extends the p=2 appendix in reference [23].
row.qualification: The attribution is contextual. The finite-exponent conclusions are proved in the repository. This row does not claim comparison of the exact 2014 edition of reference [23].

row.requirement: D.4 joint analyticity and exact roots
reviewed_claims: For each omitted integer index, the literal negative deleted product converges and is jointly analytic in the spectral parameter and the displacement.
Its zeros are exactly the retained roots, with the count of repeated retained indices as analytic multiplicity.
row.qualification: All finite p>=1 are retained. Repeated roots are allowed in this assertion, and the omitted index is removed before counting multiplicity.

row.requirement: Simple roots and reciprocal poles
reviewed_claims: For an injective root sequence the retained zeros have analytic order one.
The reciprocal is meromorphic, has order minus one at each retained root, and is the limit of the reciprocal symmetric products away from those roots.
row.qualification: The zero and pole locations are the original displaced roots, with no unmentioned nonvanishing assumption at the omitted index.

row.requirement: Paired perturbation sums and products
reviewed_claims: Opposite indices cancel the spectral parameter in the linear perturbation sum and give the exact square-denominator quadratic identity.
Both paired expressions are absolutely summable at every finite Banach exponent; the quadratic one is summable even for bounded displacements.
row.qualification: The zero entry is totalized and unused. These statements are fixed-parameter summability results; local uniformity is supplied by the next separately proved product-convergence assertion.

row.requirement: Local uniform product convergence and analyticity
reviewed_claims: Full and deleted symmetric cutoffs converge uniformly on compact spectral sets and bounded displacement sets.
Every finite cutoff is jointly analytic and its limit is jointly analytic, including p=1.
row.qualification: The proof uses uniform product estimates and exponent inclusion for the summable endpoint. It proves the required local uniform convergence without treating pointwise convergence alone as sufficient.

row.requirement: Free open quarter-pi discs
reviewed_claims: The free source discs are open balls of radius pi/4 centered at pi*n, and their exterior contains the boundaries.
row.qualification: The complement is taken after the union over every signed integer index.

row.requirement: D.5 locally uniform exterior asymptotic
reviewed_claims: The normalized full product is jointly analytic and has exactly the prescribed roots with their multiplicities.

For every displacement and epsilon>0, one positive neighborhood radius and one spectral threshold make the literal exterior error supremum smaller than epsilon for all displacements in that neighborhood.
row.qualification: This retains the strict supremum statement, the full exterior including boundaries, and every finite p>=1. The threshold is chosen before varying the displacement in the neighborhood.

row.requirement: Entire product divided by sine as a relative product
reviewed_claims: Off the free lattice the sine-normalized source product equals the actual convergent relative product.
The product error is bounded by exp of the absolute reciprocal-sum norm minus one.
row.qualification: The factors are 1-a_m/(z-pi*m), equal to the printed root ratios. The quotient is evaluated only where its sine denominator is nonzero.

row.requirement: Nearest lattice point and reciprocal denominator estimate
reviewed_claims: Each exterior point has a real nearest lattice index with real displacement at most pi/2.
For that index every reciprocal denominator satisfies the factor-four estimate, and one index works before all factors and complex numerators.
row.qualification: Use the non-strict lower distance pi/4 at exterior boundary points; the source discs are open. The factor four is retained. The nearest-index helper passed its full check and is committed and pushed.

row.requirement: Exterior reciprocal sum split into far and near indices
reviewed_claims: The actual scalar reciprocal sum converges and splits into a distant kernel plus the coefficient tail.
The two printed decay denominators hold with explicit constant 8*(4*p.toReal+1), including p=1.
row.qualification: Correct the tail to the half-radius tail retaining abs(m)>=floor(abs(n)/2)+1. The near split only provides this half-radius information. The constant and tail index are corrected directly without proving a counterexample.

row.requirement: Local uniform decay gives asymptotic
reviewed_claims: The absolute reciprocal-sum norm tends to zero at spectral infinity outside fixed free discs.
One threshold works throughout a neighborhood of any fixed displacement, yielding the required locally uniform sine asymptotic.
row.qualification: The final uniformity is proved by finite-support approximation and a common operator bound. The scalar split is also proved, but the final theorem does not depend on an unproved assertion about uniform tails over an arbitrary bounded set.

row.requirement: D.6 separated tail products with uniform constants
reviewed_claims: Two arbitrary bounded complex displacements with finite ell-p difference have genuinely convergent tail-disc relative products for finite 1<p<infinity.
One positive constant, chosen from p,c and the two norm bounds before the inputs or cutoffs, bounds both the p-power sum and the printed linear-norm right side.
row.qualification: The final theorem is stronger: it permits every cutoff beyond the separated tail and does not need simplicity or the printed small-tail condition. Where the proof uses small factors, use the separately proved uniform cutoff with c on both head and tail terms; do not retain the incomplete sufficient-condition constant.

row.requirement: Literal ratio perturbation
reviewed_claims: The actual quotient minus one is the off-diagonal displacement difference divided by the reference denominator.
Reconstructing numerator roots from their literal displacement difference gives exactly the source relative product.
row.qualification: Separation gives nonzero off-diagonal denominators before the division identity is used. The omitted product entry is one and the omitted sum entry is zero.

row.requirement: Uniform half-unit cutoff for all retained factors
reviewed_claims: The head/tail factor bound retains abs(n), the head coefficient 2*c/abs(n), and c multiplying the tail norm.
For every positive tolerance one positive cutoff works before every signed n, every point in its original disc, and every factor index; the half-unit bound follows.
row.qualification: Use signed-index magnitude and the inclusive Fourier-tail convention. The statements also hold at p=1. No source formula is disproved to establish this correction.

row.requirement: Corrected product-error inequality and its three sums
reviewed_claims: The actual product-error norm supremum is at most A*exp(S)+B*exp(S+S^2).
Here A is the supremum of the signed sum, S is the sum of the individual factor suprema and B is the sum of their squares; both factor sums converge.
row.qualification: Replace the printed equality by an inequality directly. Every supremum is over the original full open disc; no maximum-attainment assumption is imposed. A common cutoff precedes all tail indices.

row.requirement: Holder bound for absolute reciprocal sum
reviewed_claims: Holder bounds the sum of factor suprema by c times the conjugate-exponent reciprocal-kernel norm times norm(a).
row.qualification: Keep c explicit instead of hiding it in a symbol labeled C_p. The exact conjugate-kernel bound assumes 1<p<infinity, as in D.6. The zero kernel entry implements the omitted diagonal.

row.requirement: Finite head modification and signed-row estimate
reviewed_claims: Simplicity permits one finite modification of the head discs, leaving the original tail discs unchanged and giving a global off-diagonal separation.
One radius and one separation constant C are chosen before all inputs. All independent samples give genuinely convergent ell-p signed rows, with a single least norm majorant over the modified discs.
row.qualification: Retain C explicitly in the bound pi^(-1)*(HilbertBound+C*(2*norm(r)+1+pi/4)*norm(square kernel))*norm(a). Do not claim uniform finite-head control from the displacement norm alone. The original tail conclusion uses its own independently proved uniform bound.

row.requirement: Square row at p>=2
reviewed_claims: For finite p>=2, the literal sum of squared factor suprema has half-exponent membership and summable p/2 powers.
Its total p/2 energy is at most c^p*norm(a)^p times the reciprocal-square convolution constant to power p/2.
row.qualification: Young convolution gives the half-exponent estimate. The finite head is extended by zero, so the full integer sum is exactly the selected-tail sum. The two literal-square theorems passed their full check and are committed and pushed.

row.requirement: Square row at p<=2
reviewed_claims: The same literal squared-supremum sum belongs to ell-(p/2) for 1<p<=2, allowing the target exponent to be below one.
The powered bound retains c^p and the p norm of a; at p=3/2 these are c^(3/2), norm(a)^(3/2), and target exponent 3/4.
row.qualification: Correct c^2 to c^p in the powered energy and the inconsistent q norm label to p. Powered Young handles the quasi-normed range. The positive theorem passed its full check and is committed and pushed; no refutation is added.

row.requirement: Combined powered product estimate
reviewed_claims: Combining the signed row, square row and absolute bound gives the literal product-error supremum in ell-p.
The p-power sum has a constant uniform before all bounded inputs and later cutoffs, and the linear-norm version is retained as well.
row.qualification: The final constant retains dependence on c,p,the reference norm bound and the difference norm bound. The repository proves the final estimate by uniform majorants, without relying on the printed equality or missing constant labels in intermediate displays.

row.requirement: D.7 signed quadratic remainder
reviewed_claims: After subtracting the signed root-difference reciprocal sum, the literal tail-disc norm supremum belongs to ell-(p/2), uniformly on bounded input sets.
This implies the printed ell-(p/2)+ell-(1+) decomposition with one common zero second component.
row.qualification: The selected tail is extended by zero on the finite head. The half-exponent target includes p<2; the linear subtraction remains complex and signed.

row.requirement: D.8 multiplicative and additive deleted-product estimates
reviewed_claims: The literal positive deleted product divided by its omitted normalization denominator has both multiplicative and additive ell-p errors.
Actual error suprema and arbitrary independent samples share one bound throughout each displacement norm ball, hence locally uniformly.

The proof uses the existing complex-line identity argument and then derivative and series uniqueness, an alternative to the printed polarization argument. Time-derivative interpolation proves summability directly against the exact lattice reference, including its (-1)^n phase. It does not use separate printed Young estimates for each wave-shift term.

row.claim: Midpoints and Dirichlet roots are real analytic on the real source locus.

row.claim: Both G.7 estimates hold for every finite p>1 on a common open complex neighborhood, with Dirichlet half-wave index -2*n.

row.claim: The actual midpoint derivative is the isolating-contour integral of Delta*dDelta/(Delta^2-4).
row.qualification: The source derivative has the exact -1/(2*pi*i) contour formula on a common neighborhood. The formula includes collapsed gaps and its physical realization is independent of the admissible isolating circle.

reviewed_claims: The actual midpoint derivative is the isolating-contour integral of Delta*dDelta/(Delta^2-4).

row.claim: Canonical high-frequency circles and uniform contour bounds give midpoint-gradient summability.
row.qualification: The actual pi/4 circles are constructed after a common cutoff. A positive denominator lower bound yields a uniform quotient bound, the spectral supremum precedes the outer summability norm, and the operator contour estimate transfers the majorant to actual midpoint derivatives, including finite heads.

reviewed_claims: Canonical high-frequency circles and uniform contour bounds give midpoint-gradient summability.

row.claim: Simple Dirichlet roots supply the canonical eigenfunction from the sum of actual columns.
row.qualification: Simplicity and analyticity hold at every index on one source neighborhood. The physical Dirichlet eigenfunction is the actual solution with initial vector (1,1), hence the sum of the two fundamental columns; at a root its dual solution is proportional to it.
row.requirement: Simple Dirichlet roots supply the canonical eigenfunction from the sum of actual columns.
reviewed_claims: Simple Dirichlet roots supply the canonical eigenfunction from the sum of actual columns.

row.claim: The actual Dirichlet gradient is the quadratic eigenfunction product divided by its nonzero bilinear normalization.
row.qualification: The exact bilinear normalization is twice the unconjugated integral of the eigenfunction components. Simplicity proves it nonzero. The implicit derivative quotient equals the reversed squared-component gradient divided by that normalization; canonical real-source derivatives are identified without an assumed gradient formula.
row.requirement: The actual Dirichlet gradient is the quadratic eigenfunction product divided by its nonzero bilinear normalization.
reviewed_claims: The actual Dirichlet gradient is the quadratic eigenfunction product divided by its nonzero bilinear normalization.

row.claim: The gradient estimates conclude from the positive spectral and physical realization results.
row.qualification: For each finite p>1 a common complex neighborhood supports the corrected actual midpoint and normalized Dirichlet gradient sequences at every H1 source it contains. row.claim: The kth Hamiltonian on complex H^(k-1) has the actual physical integral with factor (-i)^(k+1).
row.qualification: Lean uses density index n=k-1. The new Parseval specialization identifies the literal integral for the synthesized L2 representatives on every complex source at the printed regularity, including H^0 for mass. The representative-independent version assumes only the original Fourier coefficients and L2 membership.

reviewed_claims: The kth Hamiltonian on complex H^(k-1) has the actual physical integral with factor (-i)^(k+1).

row.claim: The initial density and derivative-plus-product Riccati recurrence retain their source indices and signs.
row.qualification: The antidiagonal sum is the source sum after shifting u_(n+1) to index n. Original period-one differentiation multiplies coefficients by 2*pi*i*j. The next density at the minimal source regularity is the actual weak H^-1 recurrence.
row.requirement: The initial density and derivative-plus-product Riccati recurrence retain their source indices and signs.
reviewed_claims: The initial density and derivative-plus-product Riccati recurrence retain their source indices and signs.

row.claim: H.1 separates the kth derivative of the second field from a fixed lower-jet remainder on H^(k-1).
row.qualification: The equality holds coefficientwise, in H^-1, and in actual tempered distributions. No additional regularity is assumed. Smooth density and continuity identify the independent recurrence with the physical hierarchy.
row.requirement: H.1 separates the kth derivative of the second field from a fixed lower-jet remainder on H^(k-1).
reviewed_claims: H.1 separates the kth derivative of the second field from a fixed lower-jet remainder on H^(k-1).

row.claim: The remainder q_k is homogeneous of total weight k+1 when each field and each derivative counts once.
row.qualification: The polynomial is fixed independently of its input. The jet (field,j) has total weight j+1.
row.requirement: The remainder q_k is homogeneous of total weight k+1 when each field and each derivative counts once.
reviewed_claims: The remainder q_k is homogeneous of total weight k+1 when each field and each derivative counts once.

row.claim: Each monomial of the nonlinear Hamiltonian density has total derivative count at most k-2.
row.qualification: The bound is on the sum of derivative orders, and therefore bounds every individual jet. Integer grading retains the negative bound at k=1; the remainder is zero there.
row.requirement: Each monomial of the nonlinear Hamiltonian density has total derivative count at most k-2.
reviewed_claims: Each monomial of the nonlinear Hamiltonian density has total derivative count at most k-2.

row.claim: Every monomial of the nonlinear Hamiltonian density has equal first-field and second-field counts.
row.qualification: Field charge is the second-field count minus the first-field count. Multiplication by the first field changes the remainder charge one to zero.
row.requirement: Every monomial of the nonlinear Hamiltonian density has equal first-field and second-field counts.
reviewed_claims: Every monomial of the nonlinear Hamiltonian density has equal first-field and second-field counts.

row.claim: The original u_k polynomials have weight k and use derivatives only through k-1.
row.qualification: Canonical polynomial evaluation equals the actual smooth recurrence. The total derivative bound is stronger than the required individual jet bound, with the same shifted Lean index.
row.requirement: The original u_k polynomials have weight k and use derivatives only through k-1.
reviewed_claims: The original u_k polynomials have weight k and use derivatives only through k-1.

row.claim: Field rescaling holds for every complex scalar, including zero.
row.qualification: Recurrence uniqueness proves u_k(a,c*b)=c*u_k(c*a,b) directly. Continuity transfers it to the available Sobolev densities and the weak H^-1 boundary without dividing by c.
row.requirement: Field rescaling holds for every complex scalar, including zero.
reviewed_claims: Field rescaling holds for every complex scalar, including zero.

row.claim: The smooth real odd Hamiltonian is the top-derivative square integral plus (-1)^(m+1) times the unreduced H.1 remainder integral.
row.qualification: Adopt the exact phase from (-i)^(2m+2) directly. The same H.1 polynomial is retained before reduction; the final H.2 polynomial absorbs the phase. Historical refutations are unchanged and no new refutation is added.
row.requirement: The smooth real odd Hamiltonian is the top-derivative square integral plus (-1)^(m+1) times the unreduced H.1 remainder integral.
reviewed_claims: The smooth real odd Hamiltonian is the top-derivative square integral plus (-1)^(m+1) times the unreduced H.1 remainder integral.

row.claim: Removing a factor of derivative order m+n leaves total derivative count at most m-2-n.
row.qualification: The exact monomial grading subtracts the removed jet order from the bound 2*m-2. The integration-by-parts implementation uses this subtraction for either field, with the coefficient and all remaining factors retained.
row.requirement: Removing a factor of derivative order m+n leaves total derivative count at most m-2-n.
reviewed_claims: Removing a factor of derivative order m+n leaves total derivative count at most m-2-n.

row.claim: Repeated integration by parts lowers every nonlinear factor to derivative order at most m-1.
row.qualification: The construction records an explicit polynomial total derivative, terminates by the maximal jet order, preserves both gradings, and gives the same actual integral on every smooth periodic source.
row.requirement: Repeated integration by parts lowers every nonlinear factor to derivative order at most m-1.
reviewed_claims: Repeated integration by parts lowers every nonlinear factor to derivative order at most m-1.

row.claim: For each m>=1, one lower-jet polynomial gives H.2 for every real H^m source.
row.qualification: The polynomial is chosen before the potential and uses only jets through m-1. The leading term is the actual squared L2 weak derivative with unit-period Parseval. The full H^m domain is retained; H^(2m) is not required. The complex counterpart uses the unconjugated bilinear leading integral.
row.requirement: For each m>=1, one lower-jet polynomial gives H.2 for every real H^m source.
reviewed_claims: For each m>=1, one lower-jet polynomial gives H.2 for every real H^m source.

row.claim: The same reduced polynomial has total weight 2m+2 and balanced field counts.
row.qualification: Both gradings survive the polynomial integration-by-parts reduction and multiplication by the exact scalar phase. These properties hold for the same polynomial in the physical H.2 formula.
row.requirement: The same reduced polynomial has total weight 2m+2 and balanced field counts.
reviewed_claims: The same reduced polynomial has total weight 2m+2 and balanced field counts.

row.claim: The original Banach-space operator is represented in bounded direct-sum coordinates.
row.qualification: A bounded linear equivalence to the product identifies the original Id+T with its two-by-two block operator. The first block need not be finite dimensional at this stage.
row.requirement: The original Banach-space operator is represented in bounded direct-sum coordinates.
reviewed_claims: The original Banach-space operator is represented in bounded direct-sum coordinates.

row.claim: Assuming Id+D invertible, Id+T is invertible exactly when Id+A-B(Id+D)^(-1)C is invertible.
row.qualification: Adopt lower-block invertibility as a premise of the equivalence. The sufficient direction retains the source hypotheses. Historical counterexamples remain unchanged; this comparison adds no refutation.
row.requirement: Assuming Id+D invertible, Id+T is invertible exactly when Id+A-B(Id+D)^(-1)C is invertible.
reviewed_claims: Assuming Id+D invertible, Id+T is invertible exactly when Id+A-B(Id+D)^(-1)C is invertible.

row.claim: For a finite-dimensional first block, det S nonzero and norm(D)<1 imply invertibility.
row.qualification: The strict norm bound gives invertibility of Id+D by the Neumann argument. Under that bound the determinant criterion is also necessary, in the original Banach-space coordinates.
row.requirement: For a finite-dimensional first block, det S nonzero and norm(D)<1 imply invertibility.
reviewed_claims: For a finite-dimensional first block, det S nonzero and norm(D)<1 imply invertibility.

row.claim: Compactness is equivalent to total boundedness and completeness.
row.qualification: This is the standard metric-space compactness criterion. In the complete coefficient spaces the specialized statements use closedness; they also characterize the compact closure of an arbitrary unweighted set.
row.requirement: Compactness is equivalent to total boundedness and completeness.
reviewed_claims: Compactness is equivalent to total boundedness and completeness.

row.claim: I.3 retains arbitrary sets, raw pointwise bounds, finite p>=1 and one symmetric tail cutoff for every positive error.
row.qualification: The head is exactly |n|<=N, the tail |n|>N, and N>=1. Coefficient bounds may depend on n; no global norm bound is supplied. Every positive weight preserves the exact norm and raw coefficient interpretation.
row.requirement: I.3 retains arbitrary sets, raw pointwise bounds, finite p>=1 and one symmetric tail cutoff for every positive error.
reviewed_claims: I.3 retains arbitrary sets, raw pointwise bounds, finite p>=1 and one symmetric tail cutoff for every positive error.

row.claim: I.4 starts with a real-analytic cone map and compact complexified derivative minus identity at its source points.
row.qualification: The domain is relatively open in the nonnegative cone. Local real analytic extensions define analyticity at its boundary. Their complex germs and derivative compatibility are constructed. Compactness is assumed only at cone points. Arbitrary positive weights cover every real Sobolev order.
row.requirement: I.4 starts with a real-analytic cone map and compact complexified derivative minus identity at its source points.
reviewed_claims: I.4 starts with a real-analytic cone map and compact complexified derivative minus identity at its source points.

row.claim: One actual local real inverse provides the seed.
row.qualification: The seed is an inverse germ of the original real extension, with both inverse identities. The separately proved weaker seed is a differentiable real left inverse; it does not strengthen the printed hypotheses.
row.requirement: One actual local real inverse provides the seed.
reviewed_claims: One actual local real inverse provides the seed.

row.claim: The set of local diffeomorphism points is relatively open and dense.
row.qualification: The theorem uses preconnectedness, which is weaker than path connectedness. It gives actual real analytic inverses on ambient real neighborhoods, both identities, and recovery of the original cone map near the center. The inverse locus is independent of the atlas.
row.requirement: The set of local diffeomorphism points is relatively open and dense.
reviewed_claims: The set of local diffeomorphism points is relatively open and dense.

row.claim: Compactness of the unit-ball image yields an operator-norm output tail at most one quarter.
row.qualification: The weighted operator is the exact I.3 tail. All input columns remain present. The cutoff works for every larger N and for any positive error, including 1/4.
row.requirement: Compactness of the unit-ball image yields an operator-norm output tail at most one quarter.
reviewed_claims: Compactness of the unit-ball image yields an operator-norm output tail at most one quarter.

row.claim: Continuity improves the center quarter bound to a half bound on a complex neighborhood.
row.qualification: The complex neighborhood belongs to the constructed local extension of the original real map. The norm is the original weighted operator norm. Compactness is not assumed on that ambient complex neighborhood.
row.requirement: Continuity improves the center quarter bound to a half bound on a complex neighborhood.
reviewed_claims: Continuity improves the center quarter bound to a half bound on a complex neighborhood.

row.claim: A common cutoff works along a compact path and on neighborhoods of its points.
row.qualification: The compact-family theorem gives one cutoff on an open neighborhood whenever a continuous ambient family is given. For the actual source atlas, one cutoff gives a relative quarter bound near any compact subset and a complex half-bound neighborhood for each of its germs. The final density proof uses these intrinsic local germs and local Schur determinants; it does not assert a single globally chosen holomorphic extension along the whole path.
row.requirement: A common cutoff works along a compact path and on neighborhoods of its points.
reviewed_claims: A common cutoff works along a compact path and on neighborhoods of its points.

row.claim: The proof introduces finite-head and complementary-tail block coordinates.
row.qualification: The printed cutoff notation is compared with the exact symmetric projections. The canonical final Fredholm argument constructs a finite-dimensional invariant summand and a closed invertible complement at each point. This is an alternative local decomposition, not a claim that its summands equal the printed Fourier head and tail.
row.requirement: The proof introduces finite-head and complementary-tail block coordinates.
reviewed_claims: The proof introduces finite-head and complementary-tail block coordinates.

row.claim: The lower block acts on the tail space Y and its norm is at most the full output-tail norm.
row.qualification: Use L(Y_N), correcting the displayed L(X_N). The positive theorem constructs D on the actual range of the tail projection and proves the bound with constant one. Combining it with the half bound gives the strict premise of I.2.
row.requirement: The lower block acts on the tail space Y and its norm is at most the full output-tail norm.
reviewed_claims: The lower block acts on the tail space Y and its norm is at most the full output-tail norm.

row.claim: A nonzero finite-dimensional Schur determinant detects invertibility of the derivative.
row.qualification: The determinant is the actual determinant of the finite block. Lower-block invertibility is established before applying the criterion; no determinant of an infinite-dimensional operator is used.
row.requirement: A nonzero finite-dimensional Schur determinant detects invertibility of the derivative.
reviewed_claims: A nonzero finite-dimensional Schur determinant detects invertibility of the derivative.

row.claim: The Schur expression is Id+A-B(Id+D)^(-1)C.
row.qualification: Adopt the signs from I.1 directly in the adjacent proof display. The analytic formula is composed from the same blocks and the inverse of the invertible lower block. No new false-positive example is proved.
row.requirement: The Schur expression is Id+A-B(Id+D)^(-1)C.
reviewed_claims: The Schur expression is Id+A-B(Id+D)^(-1)C.

row.claim: The corrected Schur complement and its finite determinant are analytic.
row.qualification: Local analytic inversion gives the lower-block inverse near the center. Polynomial determinant composition gives a scalar analytic criterion. The final proof allows different local determinants at different centers.
row.requirement: The corrected Schur complement and its finite determinant are analytic.
reviewed_claims: The corrected Schur complement and its finite determinant are analytic.

row.claim: Analytic uniqueness propagates nonvanishing into every nonempty relatively open source set.
row.qualification: The cone need not have ambient interior. Agreement on its relatively open part determines the ambient analytic germ, including boundary points. A connectedness argument propagates local nonvanishing criteria without requiring one global determinant.
row.requirement: Analytic uniqueness propagates nonvanishing into every nonempty relatively open source set.
reviewed_claims: Analytic uniqueness propagates nonvanishing into every nonempty relatively open source set.

row.claim: The derivative-invertible locus is open and dense and equals the real local-inverse locus.
row.qualification: Openness follows from operator-norm continuity and openness of the units. Relative density follows from the local analytic criteria, and the real inverse theorem supplies both actual inverse identities. The conclusion includes cone boundary points.
row.requirement: The derivative-invertible locus is open and dense and equals the real local-inverse locus.
reviewed_claims: The derivative-invertible locus is open and dense and equals the real local-inverse locus.

No automatic representation of every functional on an infinity-exponent source is asserted; any use there retains its supplied-representative hypothesis.

row.requirement: Actual Dirichlet eigenvalues and sheet signs
reviewed_claims: Each actual Hilbert isospectral set is homeomorphic to the product of its signed Dirichlet gap sheets. The base coordinate is the original Dirichlet eigenvalue, and the sign is its actual anti-discriminant sign.
Every allowable full signed data family determines a unique source in that isospectral set. The two sheet branches are glued at the endpoints, where the sign is zero.
The additional assertion of nonconservation under physical NLS, and its rough description of signs as directions of NLS motion, remain outside this completed comparison.
row.qualification: The parameterization uses the original Hilbert topology and includes infinitely many open gaps and endpoint data. Indexed spectral flows are not being identified with ordinary physical NLS time. The dynamical clause remains unresolved, so this passage is partial.

row.requirement: Physical NLS nonconservation of actual Dirichlet eigenvalues
reviewed_claims: The exact classical phase satisfies the scalar physical PDE and is the constructed global ordinary solution of constant smooth data.
Literal Fourier coefficients retain the original real source and its canonical Dirichlet coordinate.
A positive physical time changes the actual central Dirichlet coordinate for a suitable real constant datum.
The trajectory satisfies the dissertation all-smooth-sequence solution definition for every 1<p<=2, including p=2.
row.qualification: Existential nonconservation of Dirichlet coordinates is proved. The rough sheet-sign direction-of-motion clause remains unresolved, so ordered group S7-002 remains partial. Indexed spectral flow is not used as physical time.

row.requirement: Physical Lax transport and exact characteristic velocity
reviewed_claims: The time Lax matrix is verified against the physical NLS vector field and the original spatial ODE. Uniqueness identifies the actual potential variation.
Periodic endpoints give the actual monodromy commutator. At a Dirichlet zero the characteristic variation equals terminal anti-discriminant times P; a simple root has velocity -delta*P/chi_prime.
For the real pair, P=2*mu^2-2*mu*Re(a(0))+abs(a(0))^2+Im(a_prime(0)).
